articles.title: Denny Hamlin makes 750th Cup start as one major career achievement still remains unfinished after two decades, 64 wins and three Daytona 500 victories
articles.summary: International Sports News: Denny Hamlin reached 750 NASCAR Cup Series starts on Saturday at Bristol Motor Speedway, becoming only the 15th driver in series history to hit the ma.
articles.body: Denny Hamlin reached 750 NASCAR Cup Series starts on Saturday at Bristol Motor Speedway, becoming only the 15th driver in series history to hit the mark. The 45-year-old Joe Gibbs Racing driver has spent his entire Cup career in the No. 11 Toyota, building a record that includes 64 wins and three Daytona 500 victories. Yet the milestone also brings back the one achievement missing from his career: a Cup Series championship. Hamlin entered Bristol leading the 2026 Chase standings, but Kyle Larson moved ahead after finishing second while Hamlin placed eighth.How did Denny Hamlin reach 750 NASCAR Cup Series starts with Joe Gibbs RacingHamlin’s 750th start came nearly 21 years after his Cup debut at Kansas Speedway in October 2005. He has driven full-time for Joe Gibbs Racing since 2006, and every one of his Cup starts has come in the No. 11 car.That kind of long-term run is unusual in NASCAR. Drivers change teams, car numbers and manufacturers over the years, but Hamlin has stayed with the same organisation throughout his Cup career. His career has also stretched across major changes in NASCAR, including different car generations and changes to the championship format.The numbers show how much he has achieved during that time. Hamlin now has 64 Cup Series wins, which ranks ninth on the all-time list. He has won the Daytona 500 three times, in 2016, 2019 and 2020. He has also won the Southern 500 three times and the Coca-Cola 600 once.Bristol has also been a strong track for him. Before his 750th start, Hamlin had four Cup wins there, including three victories in the Bristol Night Race, in 2012, 2019 and 2023.His 700th start came only 50 races earlier, at Nashville Superspeedway in June 2025. He finished third that night after leading 79 laps. Reaching 750 so soon after another major milestone shows that Hamlin is still adding to his record rather than simply looking back at it.Why is Denny Hamlin’s 750th start still linked to his missing Cup championshipFor all those wins, Hamlin has never won the NASCAR Cup Series championship.That has become one of the defining parts of his career. He has reached the Championship 4 four times, in 2014, 2019, 2020 and 2021, but each season ended without the title. He also came painfully close again last year.At the 2025 season finale at Phoenix Raceway, Hamlin entered the final race with a chance to win the championship. He led late in the race, but a late caution changed the situation and he ultimately finished second in the final standings. NASCAR’s analysis noted that Hamlin has said a championship would still mean a great deal to him, even though he is already proud of what he has achieved.“It would mean a lot personally, but also if I quit today, I’m still really happy with the stats we were able to put on the stat sheet and the wins that we’ve been able to get,” Hamlin said. “It certainly would be very gratifying. But what matters to me is my dad saw me when I was at my absolute best, and that was at Phoenix last year.”Hamlin has repeatedly put himself in position to win the title, but the single-race nature of the modern Championship 4 finale has left little room for mistakes.How strong was Denny Hamlin’s 2026 NASCAR season when he reached 750 startsHamlin did not arrive at Bristol simply to celebrate a career milestone. He was still firmly in the championship fight.Before the Bristol race, Hamlin led the Chase standings after the opening two playoff races. He had four wins, 14 top-five finishes and 18 top-10 finishes through 28 races, along with an average finish of 8.6. He had also finished on the lead lap in 27 straight races, one short of Carl Edwards’ Cup Series record.His 2026 season has included another important stretch of form. NASCAR lists his most recent victory as his June win at Pocono Raceway, where he completed a run of three straight wins in a season for the first time in his career.Bristol itself did not produce another Hamlin victory. He finished eighth in his 750th start, while Joey Logano won the race and Kyle Larson finished second. Larson’s result moved him one point ahead of Hamlin in the Chase standings.That result changed the meaning of the milestone almost immediately. Hamlin reached 750 starts, but the championship fight continued with Larson now holding the points lead.What does Denny Hamlin’s future look like after 750 NASCAR Cup startsHamlin’s career is no longer only about what he does behind the wheel. He is also a co-owner of 23XI Racing with Michael Jordan, giving him responsibilities beyond his own No. 11 car. He has also built a major presence through his podcast, where he regularly discusses NASCAR and his own experiences in the sport.Still, his driving career is far from finished. At 45, Hamlin remains one of the leading drivers in the Cup Series, and his 2026 results show that he is still capable of competing for wins and the championship.The 750-start mark also puts his career alongside some of NASCAR’s most durable names. Hamlin became the 15th driver to reach the number, with former teammate Kyle Busch becoming the 14th last year.What comes next is therefore more important than the number itself. Hamlin has already built a career with 64 wins, three Daytona 500 victories and 750 Cup starts. articles.body: Nagoya: The Indian women’s hockey team continued its relentless start to the Asian Games, cruising to another big win as it eyes a first gold at the Games since 1982.At the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium on Monday, India routed Indonesia 17-1, following Sunday’s 19-0 demolition of Uzbekistan in the campaign opener. A similar outing is expected against Thailand on Wednesday before India face their first serious test against hosts Japan on Friday.Deepika opened the scoring in the eighth minute and went on to add two more goals. Rutuja Pisal and Navneet Kaur also scored three goals apiece, while Sunelita Toppo, Lalremsiami and Sakshi Rana contributed two each. Ishika and skipper Salima Tete were the other scorers as eight Indian players sounded the boards.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule| Medal TallySavita becomes most-capped playerThe day also belonged to seasoned goalkeeper Savita, who became India’s most-capped woman player. Monday’s game was her 321st appearance for the national team, taking her past Vandana Katariya’s tally of 320.Savita, who made her Asian Games debut in Jakarta in 2018, is making her fourth and last appearance at the continental Games.While the one-sided wins have provided an ideal start, they also present a challenge of adapting quickly to a higher level of competition as the tournament progresses.“The difference in quality is just too big,” chief coach Sjoerd Marijne told TOI. “I think it will be the same against Thailand and then we have to be ready for Japan. articles.title: Gukesh shouldn’t be called No. 1: Alexei Shirov questions use of ‘World Champion’ title
articles.summary: Chess News: Alexei Shirov believes chess should rethink the way it uses the term “World Champion”, suggesting the sport could adopt a system similar to tennis.The.
articles.body: Alexei Shirov believes chess should rethink the way it uses the term “World Champion”, suggesting the sport could adopt a system similar to tennis.The Spanish grandmaster made the comments while discussing India’s D Gukesh and the status attached to the classical world title.“Nothing against Gukesh, maybe we shouldn’t use words like World Champion. Chess should be like tennis,” Shirov said.Gukesh became the youngest undisputed world champion after defeating Ding Liren in the 2024 World Championship match in Singapore. He is currently the reigning FIDE world champion.Shirov’s comments come amid an ongoing debate in chess over what the title of world champion represents in a sport where players compete across several formats and events throughout the year.Unlike tennis, where Grand Slam champions are identified by their individual tournament victories and there is no single player officially recognised as the world champion, classical chess has a designated world champion determined through the FIDE championship cycle.Shirov, a former world championship candidate himself, has previously been involved in the title race. He defeated Vladimir Kramnik in a 1998 qualification match to earn the right to challenge Garry Kasparov, but the proposed world championship match between Kasparov and Shirov never took place.His remarks come during the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, where Gukesh is representing the reigning champions India.In the sixth round, India suffered a 1.5-2.5 defeat to hosts Uzbekistan in the first major clash between the top contenders. Nihal Sarin lost to Nodirbek Yakubboev, while Gukesh drew with Shamsiddin Vokhidov. R Praggnanandhaa and Arjun Erigaisi also drew their games against Nodirbek Abdusattorov and Javokhir Sindarov respectively.The defeat left India on 10 match points, while Uzbekistan moved to 12 and took sole possession of the lead.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Zach Ertz Can Make Major Franchise History Upon Return to Philadelphia Eagles
articles.summary: Veteran tight end Zach Ertz returns to the Philadelphia Eagles with a major franchise milestone within reach.The Eagles signed Ertz to their practice squad f...
articles.body:
Veteran tight end Zach Ertz returns to the Philadelphia Eagles with a major franchise milestone within reach.

The Eagles signed Ertz to their practice squad following the news that Dallas Goedert would be sidelined for several weeks with a knee injury, and he could quickly be promoted to the active roster.

Zach Ertz Needs Just 11 Catches to Become Philadelphia Eagles' All-Time Leader

Now that he's back in Philadelphia, Ertz, who previously played for the Eagles from 2013 to 2021, needs just 11 receptions to pass Harold Carmichael to become the franchise's all-time leader in catches. Carmichael had 589 total receptions in an Eagles uniform. Ertz currently sits at 579.

Ertz also sits 179 yards from tying wide receiver Mike Quick for the fourth-most receiving yards in franchise history.

It remains to be seen how much on-field opportunity Ertz will really get upon his return to the Eagles, but if he does receive some legitimate burn, he could quickly move up the franchise history books in a couple of categories.

How Much Gas Does Zach Ertz Have Left in the Tank?

The biggest question about Ertz, 35, now that he's back in Philly is how much gas he has left in the tank. After all, the guy has played 13 seasons in the league and has a lot of wear-and-tear on his body. Plus, he's coming off of a season-ending ACL tear in his right knee that he suffered last December as a member of the Washington Commanders . It remains to be seen how he'll respond to that major injury at this latter stage of his career.

But before the injury, he was still a productive player. Ertz started in 13 games for Washington last season and tallied 50 receptions for 504 yards and four touchdowns. He started in all 17 games for the Commanders the previous season and caught 66 passes for 654 yards and seven TDs.

If he can bounce back from the ACL tear, Ertz could potentially provide Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts with another option in the passing game during Goedert's absence.

articles.title: Rams 28, Giants 6: Instant position-by-position grades for New York
articles.summary: The Giants lose 28-6 against the Los Angeles Rams, but their injuries might prove to be a bigger loss.
articles.body:
The New York Giants lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart on their first offensive drive, and they failed to gain much offensive rhythm after Dart's seven offensive plays that went for 27 yards. New York failed to get anything going on the ground, and Jameis Winston looked overmatched in relief of Dart. The Giants only had 182 yards on offense, and the Rams rumbled for 481 yards, while averaging eight yards per play.

Los Angeles went 5 of 9 on third down and the Giants 3 of 14. The Rams had the football for five minutes and ten seconds more, but their explosive plays complied, as the Giants' offense sputtered all night after Dart's injury. The Giants suffered multiple injuries in the loss, but they'll have to quickly regroup on a short week. Brian Burns hurt his ankle late in the fourth quarter. It was just a brutal game for the Giants from many perspectives. Here are the grades.

The Giants lost Jaxson Dart on their first offensive drive. Dart was ruled out in the second half, and it was a devastating blow to the Giants' nation. Jameis Winston looked lost through the first half. He went 4 of 12 for 58 yards with a terrible interception in the red zone. Winston didn't improve until the Rams were up by three-plus scores well into the second half. Winston finished 11 of 27 for 111 yards while suffering two sacks and throwing an interception. It was the worst I've seen Winston as a Giant. Dart was 3 of 5 for 20 yards before the injury.

Jevon Holland forced a fumble late in the first half, which gave the Giants excellent field position and a chance to split the Rams' lead in half. Matt Nagy decided to roll out a package with Najee Harris on second and third down, with the third down play being in 11 personnel. It was a handoff, too, and it was a massive tackle for a loss that led to a Dominic Zvada 24-yard field goal. With no Jaxson Dart, Nagy kept his best running back on the bench in a critical situation – that's a HIGHLY questionable situation.

The Giants averaged a measly 2.5 yards per carry. Skattebo finished with 12 carries for 36 yards; he added four catches for 19 yards. There was no room on the ground, and the backs couldn't get much goiung.

The loss of Dart hurt the offense, and Malik Nabers battling a shoulder injury that held him out for several plays didn't help the overall chances of the Giants to win the game. The Giants offense went into a shell once Winston entered the game. Darnell Mooney had a few plays over the middle of the field, but the receivers were not receiving quality looks from Winston.

Mooney led the Giants with 48 receiving yards on two catches, while Fields hauled in two balls for 30 yards. Odell Beckham Jr. was not targeted, and Malik Nabers caught one of his four targets for one yard, and left in the first half with a shoulder injury. He returned, but the game got out of hand.

Dart's injury stifled their passing attack. Theo Johnson had an opportunity to secure a Dart pass on the play he was injured. Johnson did an excellent job high-pointing the football over two defenders, which was very impressive, but, unfortunately, Johnson could not secure the football. Isaiah Likely was targeted ten times and caught five for 33 yards.

Jon Runyan 's holding penalty ended an early potential scoring drive for the Giants. The offensive line struggled all night. They opened a few lanes for Cam Skattebo and the Giants' rushing attack, and their pass protection was suspect. Obviously, the injury to Dart changed the Giants' game plan, but the offensive line was just getting beat by the Rams' front. John Michael Schmitz , just like last week with Devin Singletary against man coverage, was late to his assignment at the second level and a screen ended in a loss, when a massive gain was attainable if that block was executed. Jermaine Eleumunor was beat bad by Byron Young on a valuable third-down in the third quarter, which led to Zvada's second field goal of the game.

Chauncey Golston forced a holding penalty and had a few disruptive plays up front, and the Rams weren't establishing the run too well for much of the game, but Stafford had too much time to pass too often. A lot of the Rams' rushing success was to the outside, and D.J. Reader had a few nice STOPs near the line of scrimmage. Still, the line didn't do enough to make a difference.

Matt Stafford had WAY too much time in the first half. He sat comfortably in the pocket and delivered too many passes beyond 20-yards. New York HAS to receive more from their pass-rush. Carter did sack Stafford by splitting a double-team, but the Giants' surrendered 21 yards on the following play to Terrance Ferguson . The Giants were also shaky on the edge against the heavier personnel packaged Rams.

Kayvon Thibodeaux lost contain on a 21-yard Williams scamper in the third quarter. New York surrendered the edge several times in the second half. What's possibly most consequential from the game is the injury to Brian Burns, who got rolled up on in garbage time. The Giants need to get more from this position group.

Kyren Williams caught a touchdown as the third receiver releasing to the boundary toward the two receiver side. Arvell Reese stayed tight toward the in breaking route of the No. 2 receiver, and Reese allowed Williams to find a soft-spot between himself and Colton Hood, where Williams caught the ball for an easy score. This was Reese's second mistake in coverage that resulted in a touchdown. The Terrance Ferguson touchdown was over the head of Tremiane Edmunds.

The middle of the field was more vulnerable versus the pass as well. Stafford found back side dig routes and other in-breaking routes in front of over-pursuing safeties, but just behind linebackers. The coverage was an F for the Giants' linebackers, but they were adequate against the run. Edmunds did, however, knock a pass away as a blitzer late in the third quarter.

Matt Stafford and Davante Adams were having success against quality cover plays by Greg Newsome III and other Giants' cornerbacks. Colton Hood wasn't terrible, but there were plays where he looked like a rookie, specifically the Davante Adams touchdown pass in the third quarter in the red zone. Greg Newsome III was forced to shadow Adams after Hood surrendered the touchdown.

Tyler Nubin had a beautiful tackle at the line of scrimmage early in the first quarter, but he was the defender that contacted Davante Adams on the veteran's first quarter touchdown. Nubin was then toasted in coverage on Matt Stafford's long 64 yards third-and-nine conversion; the third-year safety bit on an Adams' double-move. Nubin lost leverage and over-pursued on several other coverage snaps.

Jevon Holland, however, was one of the biggest difference makers for the Giants' defense. He intercepted Matt Stafford as the middle-of-the-field closed safety and then punched the football loose from Kyren Williams on the subsequent Rams' drive. Holland is living up to the off-season hype. Holland than forced a fumble against Blake Corum in the fourth quarter.

It's strange to give a grade to the safety position with Holland having a great game but Nubin having one of the worst by a Giants' safety in some time. Let's split the diff and give the position a C. Nubin was attacked all game, but he did knock one pass away from Ferguson late in the third quarter, although Nubin was beaten on the play.

Jordan Stout is an asset. Poor blocking up front forced Stout to punt it into the end zone on the Giants' second drive, but he was lucky to get the football off; his third punt, though, sailed for 61 yards. Stout also booted a 58-yarder after the Giants' failed first drive of the second half. Field position becomes more important when injuries take effect on offense. Unfortunately for the Giants, that happened early in the game.

Malachi Fields did an excellent job making a tackle after a quality punt by Jordan Stout in the second quarter. Dominic Zvada went 2 of 2 with 24 and 52 yard field goals. Stout may have been the Giants' most valuable player outside of Holland; he added a fourth quarter 78-yard punt.

articles.title: Davante Adams outgained and outscored the Giants by himself Monday
articles.summary: Davante Adams put up more yards and points than the Giants had as a team, showing just how crazy his performance was on Monday.
articles.body:
On Monday night, Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams was simply spectacular. He dismantled the New York Giants in the Rams' 28-6 win at SoFi Stadium, turning back the clock with a vintage outing. To say Adams was brilliant would be doing his performance a disservice; he dazzled on the big stage of prime time.

A player built for the bright lights, Adams showed why he's a future Hall of Famer, plucking passes out of the sky on his way towards an eight-catch, 195-yard game with two touchdowns. Just how dominant was Adams? He put up more yards himself (195) than the entire Giants offense (182).

Adams also scored 12 points, twice as many as the Giants' six. To make his performance stand out even more, he did this with Puka Nacua and Jordan Whittington missing the game due to injury. The Giants knew where the ball was going, and they couldn't do a thing about it.

Adams now has 11 receptions for 221 yards and two touchdowns this season. He will take on the Denver Broncos and former Defensive Player of the Year Pat Surtain II in Week 3. They have a long-standing history, going back to Adams' time with the Las Vegas Raiders , so Davante knows it'll be a challenge.

Daniel Jeremiah shared praise of Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence on the "Move the Sticks" podcast , insisting that Lawrence has quickly changed the narrative about the team's defense early in the season.

The Enquirer's Kelsey Conway wrote that, as Jeremiah suggested, Lawrence's impact went beyond the stat sheet.

"Three tackles, a TFL and a quarterback hit doesn't tell the story," Jeremiah said. "This was just utter dominance. Like he's in a tilted nose a lot, so lined up right over the center. You'll see him just stack doubles. You can't move him. They try and run outside zone to each side. He beats the cutoff block each time, including on one was … a fourth down . He gets a tackle for loss there."

Cincinnati Bengals vs. Houston Texans, photos from NFL Week 2

"They couldn't block him the entire game in the run game," Jeremiah continued. "It's just a wall in there, and then when you get into the pass rush stuff, you see a snatch where he just presses out and then just snatches to the ground. You see steady pocket push and you just think okay, it's all power. It's just this big guy who's almost 400 pounds. I gotta brace for power and then all of a sudden he hits you with a little club swim move and you're like, 'What the heck did that come from?'"

"He gets a pressure on a loop stunt as big as he is," Jeremiah added. "So he was all over the place and then my favorite maybe of all he zone-drops out and he's in like the middle of the field and almost gets his hand on a football. That is a very large man doing things like that. There's a very select club of guys that have that size and skillset."

Dexter Lawrence is 'perfect thing' for Bengals' matchups with Ravens

"These guys are so hard to find and he has completely changed this Bengals' defense," Jeremiah concluded. "It looks like Cincinnati and Baltimore (are) headed towards a collision and who's better equipped to help you as a player against Derrick Henry and then also to be able to collapse the pocket against Lamar Jackson like Dexter Lawrence is kind of the perfect thing for them to match up with the Baltimore Ravens , so I'm looking forward to those in the future."

The Bengals shared video of a miked-up Lawrence during the team's Week 2 win , screaming to the Texans , "You're blessed to be on this field with me. You're blessed!"

articles.title: Japan break Indian hearts as PV Sindhu, Unnati Hooda and Tanvi Sharma lose in Asian Games quarterfinal
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India's women's badminton team bowed out of the Asian Games after Japan secured a 3-1 victory in the quarterfinals on Tuesday, with the singles player.
articles.body: India's women's badminton team bowed out of the Asian Games after Japan secured a 3-1 victory in the quarterfinals on Tuesday, with the singles players unable to match the impact of the country's World Championships bronze-winning doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand.India were handed a difficult start when two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu took on world No.3 Akane Yamaguchi in the opening singles. Sindhu fought hard and took the first game 23-21, but Yamaguchi gradually took control of the contest to win the next two games 21-18, 21-6.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule |Medal TallySindhu fights back before Yamaguchi takes controlSindhu trailed 13-17 in the opening game but produced a strong recovery to move ahead. The contest featured several long rallies, with exchanges often stretching to 35-36 shots.The Indian had a game point but a wrong judgement on a back-line call gave Yamaguchi an opportunity to stay in contention. Sindhu earned another game point after Yamaguchi found the net and then finished the game with a cross-court forehand winner.Yamaguchi responded after the change of ends, establishing a two-point advantage at the mid-game interval. Sindhu again attempted to fight back after falling 12-17 behind, but the Japanese shuttler held firm to take the second game 21-18.The deciding game proved one-sided. Yamaguchi opened up a 14-6 lead and went on to earn 10 match points before sealing victory with a precise return.Miyazaki puts Japan in commandIndia needed Unnati Hooda to level the tie, but the youngster was unable to overcome 2022 world junior champion and current world No.7 Tomoka Miyazaki.Miyazaki controlled the contest to secure a 21-16, 21-18 victory, leaving Japan just one win away from the semifinals and putting India 0-2 behind.Treesa-Gayatri keep India aliveIndia's World Championships bronze-winning duo of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand then delivered when the team needed them most.Fresh from winning their maiden World Championships bronze in New Delhi, Treesa and Gayatri defeated Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto 21-17, 21-16 in the first doubles match.The victory reduced the deficit to 1-2 and briefly kept India's hopes of completing a comeback alive.Okuhara seals Japan's place in semisThe decisive match, however, went Japan's way.Young Indian shuttler Tanvi Sharma faced former world champion Nozomi Okuhara but could not find a response to her opponent's game. Okuhara won 21-12, 21-10 to give Japan an unassailable 3-1 lead.The result brought India's women's badminton team campaign at the Asian Games to an end, despite the strong showing from Treesa and Gayatri and Sindhu's spirited opening-game fight against Yamaguchi.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: SAI ramps up logistical support for Indian contingent at 2026 Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: New Delhi: The Sports Authority of India (SAI) has rolled out a series of logistical and operational support measures for the Indian contingent at the.
articles.body: New Delhi: The Sports Authority of India (SAI) has rolled out a series of logistical and operational support measures for the Indian contingent at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, aiming to ensure athletes can focus on competition throughout the Games.Working alongside the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), the Embassy of India in Japan and the Games Organising Committee, SAI has stationed a dedicated reception and assistance team at the airport to welcome athletes, coaches and support staff arriving in Japan. At the onset of the Games, Indian diaspora had also stepped in to come to the assistance of the athletes if required.The team is assisting the contingent with immigration and arrival formalities, providing refreshments and guiding members to their accommodation and competition venues.Among the key initiatives is dedicated transport for India's shooting squad, with vehicles arranged to ferry athletes to and from competition venues. SAI has also deployed cars for medical personnel, allowing them to move quickly between venues and provide timely assistance to athletes.To address accommodation constraints, the organisation has secured additional rooms for coaches and support staff who could not be housed by the Games organisers because of limited availability.Double Asian Games 2026 medallist Rudrankksh Patil had spoken about accommodation issues he and his other shooting contingent faced in Aichi-Nagoya.Patil highlighted that the contingent had to wait for hours for their bus to arrive at the airport, and then the coaches had a disagreement with the hotel staff after they were not offered the hotel they booked their rooms in."We went to the welcoming centre. It took us three hours to wait for the bus over there. At 2 or 3 am, we started leaving for the hotel and reached there at around 3:30 or 4 am. After reaching the hotel, we realised that the hotel we had booked was not our hotel, we only had a couple of rooms over there, and that was supposed to be the best hotel," said Patil."And our coaches were fighting over there that if you can give us the confirmation for the best hotel, then how are you shifting us to some other hotel?" he added.The coordinated support forms part of SAI's efforts to provide seamless logistical, medical and operational assistance at the continental showpiece in Japan.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Wigan Warriors focused on taking on 'battle-hardened' Wakefield Trinity for spot in Super League Grand Final
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors are well versed in making it to the Super League Grand Final and that means being focused on one step at a time; watch Wigan Warriors vs Wakefield Trinity in the Super League semi-finals live on Sky Sports on Saturday September 26, with kick-off at 5.30pm
articles.body:
Wigan have already added two trophies to their cabinet this season having won the Challenge Cup and League Leaders' Shield, with the Grand Final just one step away.

To get there, they need to beat Wakefield in the semi-finals on Saturday September 26, live on Sky Sports after Daryl Powell's side defeated Leigh in the eliminators.

Matt Peet lost a first final as head coach of Wigan at Old Trafford in 2025 against Hull KR, but has already made sure that such heartbreak was fuel to achieve more.

But now, with success firmly in their sights once again, Wigan will keep looking forward while being rooted in the present and ensuring they are firmly focused on the semi-finals.

"We have been through this experience a few times now, learned some lessons, and it is exciting," Peet told Sky Sports .

"It is not a case of that everything we did last year was wrong, some things we got right, we just weren't good enough on the evening.

"We will do what is right for this year's team for this moment on their journey and our journey.

"It is more about looking forward than back."

If Wigan were to win the Grand Final, it would mark Peet's 10th trophy since taking over as head coach of his hometown club in 2022, success coming under him at a staggering speed.

However, those statistics are of no importance to him and the most important trophy is always the one next in your sights.

"It is not about that, the next one is always the one," he added.

"We just want to play well in the semi-finals. Not thinking too much about Old Trafford or the trophy or talking about that.

"We know we are going to be up against a very determined and capable team in the semi-finals who have just had a fantastic win.

"They will be battle-hardened and confident so we just have to concern ourselves with that."

O'Neill: Ready to right heartbreak of 2025

2025 was a particularly unique year for Wigan under Peet. They made finals but did not win them as Hull KR swept every honour available.

They also fell to a tough 24-6 loss in the Grand Final, which saw Brad O'Neill sent to the sin-bin for a dangerous tackle.

O'Neill has been one of Wigan's standout performers across 2026, being named in the Super League Dream Team, and would love to right that wrong.

Indeed, he feels they have put themselves in the best possible position to do exactly that.

"I feel like going away together pre the semi-final when we get the week off is a great opportunity to get some work in but also a good time to bond as well and get away and fresh. Just to enjoy each other's company," O'Neill told Sky Sports .

"We have done it for the last few years and everyone seems to like it.

"I feel like it would mean a lot. Last year was a tough one to take at Old Trafford for myself personally and for the club.

"To put those wrongs right would mean a lot to us all.

"We have given ourselves the best opportunity to do it, we just have to commit now and get through this semi-final first."

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Go for gold! Saurav Ghosal identifies India's biggest challenge, and incentive
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: New Delhi: For the first time in 24 years, Saurav Ghosal will watch an Asian Games from the sidelines. The former India No. 1, whose first appearance .
articles.body: New Delhi: For the first time in 24 years, Saurav Ghosal will watch an Asian Games from the sidelines. The former India No. 1, whose first appearance in the continental event came in Busan 2002, stepped away after nine medals: two gold, two silver and five bronze. But he did so with one lingering regret: no singles gold medal.Now, his role has changed. Ghosal is a mentor to teenage sensation Anahat Singh, who carries India's gold medal hopes to Aichi-Nagoya. With squash also offering direct qualification to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics for its gold medallists, the stakes are higher than ever.In a conversation with TimesofIndia.com, Ghosal reflected on watching instead of playing, preparing Anahat for the biggest tournament of her young career, and why India should judge this squad by medals — not merely potential."I wish I was there. I wish I was still playing. Kind of the best times of your life, of my life at least," Ghosal said of missing his first Asian Games since 2002.For Ghosal, the Asian Games always stood apart from the professional tour -- not because of the attention it attracts, but because of what it represents."It's more to kind of have the honour to play for India, win for India and be proud doing that. I think that kind of makes it internally something which is bigger than a normal event," he admitted.I wish I was there. I wish I was still playing. Kind of the best times of your life, of my life at leastThe straight knockout format, he added, leaves little room for error."You kind of need to be laser-focused at these events because one bad day can destroy the entire event. Especially in a sport like ours where it's straight knockouts. So you focus on yourself, focus on the things that you need to do well. And you focus on both what you do on court and off court. That's equally important in an event where it's quite long as well, which is different to what we do on the professional tour. I think all those things are things that you focus on more rather than things that can happen outside of your bubble," he explained.Anahat's gold medal preparations: Clarity over changeEighteen-year-old Anahat Singh enters the Games after a remarkable rise that has made her one of India's genuine medal contenders. Rather than altering her game, Ghosal says the focus has been on tactical clarity against specific opponents."She's a well-rounded player overall. I think it's about understanding who you're playing in this event, what your opposition is going to look like, trying to get extreme clarity on how you're going to play them, how you respond to what they're going to do to you and do so in a manner that works in your favour," said 40-year-old Ghosal.Execution, he believes, is the difference between preparation and performance."There is no guarantee that it will work out. But you have to put the building blocks in place in your mind to be able to have a chance to produce it on court," he reasoned.Anahat arrives carrying expectations few Indian teenagers have faced in squash. Ghosal's advice is rooted in the mindset that sustained him throughout his own career."The good thing about her is that she's quite carefree. She's a happy-go-lucky person. So that helps. I think that's helped her through the years. The expectations go back to the same thing that it's not in your control. And it's all about perception," said Ghosal."When I was playing, I always thought that if there was expectation, that means people actually believed in me. And that means I had something about me (that) I was actually good enough. It was almost like a re-emphasis of the belief that I had in myself that, 'OK, I might actually be good enough to do this.'"The key, he says, is preventing the mind from drifting towards outcomes."If you just think of it on those lines when you're playing, it's a bit like fooling your mind a little bit with all the necessary information there is to kind of occupy it so that you don't have time to think about, 'Oh, what if I don't win a medal?' Because that is not going to help you win. That is not going to help you play better."You almost crowd your mind with all the things that you need to do to play well. And it's almost like the antithesis of an idle mind is a devil's workshop"So you almost crowd your mind with all the things that you need to do to play well. And it's almost like the antithesis of an idle mind is a devil's workshop."So you don't want that mind to be idle in a negative way. You want that mind to be calm, but you still want things to be going on in your mind which are related to you playing better. And that's things that you do on court, but also off court. It's helped me over the years and that's what we're telling Anahat to do as well," he added.Genuine contenders and an Olympic opportunityFormer India coach Major Maniam has labelled both Anahat and Abhay Singh as genuine medal hopes, a view Ghosal shares."There's no doubt that both of them come into these Games as genuine medal contenders. It would be disappointing for them personally if they didn't win a medal at least."The bigger prize, however, is gold. Under the qualification system, the Asian Games singles champion earns a direct place at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where squash will make its Olympic debut.Ghosal acknowledges that the Olympic incentive makes the tournament "definitely bigger" but insists it isn't a daily talking point within the camp."It would be disappointing for them personally if they didn't win a medal at least. Obviously, the big prize at these Asian Games is the gold because that gives you the Olympic qualification spot. And that obviously is the big one. And it's hard and rightfully so. Getting an Olympic qualification spot shouldn't come easy."The idea obviously is that whether Anahat wins this or doesn't win it, she is going to gun for the Olympics. And when you get to the Olympics, you want to try and win something. So it's a journey that has to happen. Even if she wins the gold here and gets in the Olympics, it doesn't stop there because that doesn't guarantee you anything. It guarantees you being there, but you're not going to be there just to make up the numbers. You're going to be there to try and do something. So I think that journey continues," added Saurav.The target: Medal in every eventIndia entered the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou with eight members, clinching five medals, including two golds. Alongside Malaysia, India were joint-top in squash medals at the continental showpiece. Three years later, Ghosal stopped short of calling it the deepest team ever, but he leaves little ambiguity about the standard it should meet."Sport is black and white, right? There's no subjectivity. I think medals are the most objective barometer, to be honest. We should medal as a bare minimum in every event that we are in."So, women's singles, men's singles, mixed doubles and both team events. I think that's a bare minimum. I think if we don't medal in any of those, that's a disappointment. What would really take it to another level is the number of golds that we can get.His ambitious target is even higher."Let's say three golds. And one of them is in the singles… if we're able to do that, then it's a cracker of Games for Indian squash. It's not like we're being unrealistic, but it's not easy," he concluded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'De repente', Sergio Ramos aparece por la sede de Ferrari
articles.standfirst: El ex jugador del Real Madrid ha compartido el redes sociales las imágenes de su paso por Maranello, a donde no solo ha acudido como aficionado al motor
articles.summary: El ex jugador del Real Madrid ha compartido el redes sociales las imágenes de su paso por Maranello, a donde no solo ha acudido como aficionado al motor
articles.body: La sede de Ferrari, en Maranello, ha recibido la visita de una estrella. No se trata en esta ocasión de Hamilton ni Leclerc, sino del español Sergio Ramos, que ha acudido al mayor centro neurálgico de las pasiones automovilísticas en calidad de aficionado al mundo del motor, pero sobre todo en el papel de comprador. El de Camas ha publicado las imágenes de su visita en su cuenta de Instagram con un mensaje que reconoce el legado de la marca italiana: "poder conocer Maranello desde dentro fue una experiencia que disfruté especialmente... Cada pieza es una historia de tradición y atención al detalle que percibí desde el primer momento. Me impresionó ver cómo una casa con tanta trayectoria mantiene intacta su identidad y su compromiso con la calidad…! Una visita que me dejó mucha admiración por el trabajo y el legado que hay detrás!!!" La visita del ex jugador de Real Madrid y Sevilla no se trata de un acto de cortesía por parte de la marca ni de un acto improvisado a iniciativa del español. Se encuadra en la posibilidad que ofrece Ferrari a todos aquellos que quieren un Ferrari personalizado, posibilidad que hace realidad por medio de su departamento Atelier. Este proceso, por el que también pasó Carlos Sainz cuando encargó su Ferrari F12 Competizione y Daytona SP3, supone acudir a Maranello y sentarse con los expertos de la marca, que ofrecen un universo de posibilidades y atienden cada petición en cuanto a colores, materiales del interior... En este caso, además, Ramos pudo vivir este proceso junto a Flavio Manzoni, el diseñador jefe de la marca italiana. Aunque las imágenes de aquella visita las acaba de subir a su cuenta de Instagram, no se sabe si pertenecen a finales del año pasado, cuando encargó un 12cilindri en rojo con una banda negra central e interior en crema clara, o bien son el fruto de un algún nuevo encargo con el que ya podría haber engrosado su garaje. Porque, de hecho, se le ha podido ver sentado en un espectacular 849 Testarossa de color azul, un modelo que hereda el nombre y la filosofía del mítico Testarossa de los años 80 y que está animado por un V8 turboalimentado y tres motores eléctricos para alcanzar 1.050 CV. Si el coche es suyo, tendrá que haber desembolsado más de medio millón de euros para llevárselo.

articles.title: India defeat Sri Lanka by 147 runs as Mandhana shines in Asian Games final
articles.summary: Sri Lanka were bowled out for 69 runs, 10 less than Mandhana’s belligerent match-winning innings as India retained gold.
articles.body:
Smriti Mandhana’s whirlwind innings of 79 runs helped India crush Sri Lanka by 147 runs and win a second consecutive women’s cricket gold at the Asian Games.

India smashed 216-3 off their 20 overs, the highest women’s total in Asian Games history, with 18 fours and 13 sixes in the final on Tuesday.

Richa Ghosh and Bharti Fulmali plundered 25 off the final over from the hapless Mithali Ayodhya, who did not help her cause by conceding eight wides.

Sri Lanka were never in the hunt, and captain Chamari Athapaththu’s 29 was their only innings of note as they were skittled for 69 in 15.4 overs and had to settle for silver.

Opening batter Mandhana hit seven sixes and five fours in a 45-ball knock that sent the ball to all parts of the Korogi Athletic Park ground in Nagoya.

After India captain Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and opted to bat, Shafali Verma, who made an unbeaten century in the semifinal, and Mandhana put on a blistering opening partnership.

The pair had raced to 99 in the 10th over when Verma had a rush of blood, playing a needless reverse sweep which she top-edged to Kawya Kavindi at point to fall for 48 off 29 balls.

Mandhana, the greatest run-scorer in women’s T20 cricket history, had reached her fifty earlier in the over and sailed on in style, clubbing anything loose to the boundary.

Harmanpreet joined her, and the pair took the score to 141 before the captain holed out to long-off for 19.

Mandhana, looking to accelerate further in the latter overs, skied an attempted six and was out in the 17th over with the score on 163.

Ghosh clattered 49 off 22 balls with three sixes and six fours to take India past 200 in the final over.

Earlier, some late-order hitting by Pakistan captain Fatima Sana set up a 31-run win over Bangladesh in the bronze medal match.

Sana came in with her side rocking at 67-5 in the 12th over but plundered 45 off 30 balls, including three fours and three sixes, and was out off the last ball of the 20 overs after seeing Pakistan to 145-8.

Her 67-run partnership with Aliya Riaz (25) for the sixth wicket proved the turning point, and Bangladesh could only muster 114-7 in reply.

articles.title: Attacked with stones, trained disguised as a man: Afghan women cyclist Fariba Hashimi wins Asian Games silver
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Afghan cyclist Fariba Hashimi, who disguised herself as a man to pursue cycling as a teenager, won the silver medal in the women's road race at the As.
articles.body: Afghan cyclist Fariba Hashimi, who disguised herself as a man to pursue cycling as a teenager, won the silver medal in the women's road race at the Asian Games in Japan on Tuesday and said she hopes her achievement inspires women in Afghanistan.The 23-year-old, who is now based in Italy, finished second in the race near Nagoya and described the medal as "something special"."I can't explain my feelings now," Hashimi said after winning silver, as quoted by news agency AFP.She recalled how she began cycling with her sister Yulduz in Afghanistan, where she was attacked with stones and trained while disguised as a man."I was born inside a country where the women who dream are getting attacked, and I'm really happy that I have fought against that," she said."I hope that the next generation will come here and represent their country without any fear."Hashimi left Afghanistan after the Taliban returned to power in 2021. Since then, the Taliban authorities have imposed a series of restrictions on women, including limiting their access to education, public life and sport."They took away our freedom, they took away everything from us," Hashimi said."This silver medal can show a lot of resilience from Afghan women, and I'm really happy."I'm not alone, I know that behind me millions of women, from many countries, have the same dream and they are standing with me."Hashimi was helped to leave Afghanistan by Italian former world champion Alessandra Cappellotto and later moved to Italy, where she now lives and trains.She and her sister represented Afghanistan at the Paris Olympics two years ago, and she is now looking ahead to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics."I never want to give up and hopefully we can see (what can happen) again in Los Angeles," she said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: International Sports News: Isack Hadjar has been cleared to return to Formula 1 action for Red Bull Racing at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The French driver has successfully recov.
articles.body: Isack Hadjar has been cleared to return to Formula 1 action for Red Bull Racing at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The French driver has successfully recovered from the wrist injury that kept him out of the last three races. He will now be back alongside Max Verstappen at the Baku City Circuit, ending a 58-day wait since his last Grand Prix appearance.Hadjar last raced at the Hungarian Grand Prix in July before his injury forced him to miss Zandvoort, Monza and the all-new Madring. His return also means Liam Lawson will move back to Racing Bulls after replacing him at Red Bull, while Yuki Tsunoda returns to reserve duties.Isack Hadjar returns after three-race absenceRed Bull confirmed Isack Hadjar’s return on Tuesday after the 21-year-old completed his rehabilitation. The team had taken a cautious approach because of the demands placed on an F1 driver’s wrists.“Oracle Red Bull Racing is delighted to welcome Isack back this weekend. Having made a successful recovery from his wrist injury, Isack will return to action at the Baku City Circuit on Thursday. The team would like to sincerely thank Liam for his professionalism, dedication and hard work over the past three races”, read a statement issued by Red Bull on Tuesday.“Stepping in under challenging circumstances, he delivered some impressive performances and made a valuable contribution to the team. We wish him all the best as he returns to Visa Cash App Racing Bulls”, the statement read.Hadjar sustained the injury while training during the summer break. He was then forced to sit out three consecutive Grands Prix. He remained involved with the team during his absence but could not compete from inside the car.The Frenchman admitted that the period away from racing was difficult, “I’m really looking forward to getting back into my car. The last month has been difficult for me. It’s the first time in my life that I haven’t been racing, and it’s a strange feeling that I’ve had to get used to.”Hadjar also thanked team principal Laurent Mekies and the Red Bull team for giving him enough time to recover properly.Red Bull had been assessing Hadjar’s fitness on a race-by-race basis. The priority was to ensure that he was fully recovered before allowing him back into the car.A wrist injury can be particularly difficult for an F1 driver because of the physical demands of steering. Drivers also need to protect their hands and wrists during crashes.Hadjar’s return will also bring another change to the Red Bull driver line-up. Lawson, who stepped in for the injured driver, will return to Racing Bulls. Tsunoda will once again take up reserve duties.The Azerbaijan weekend will also follow an unusual schedule. articles.body:
Chatter about which AEW and WWE performers will be the next to jump ship has become an all-too-common theme for wrestling fans over the last year, as more and more contracts are terminated or not renewed.

With the arrival of The New Level in AEW and rumors swirling that Ilja Dragunov has also joined the company, speculation is running rampant about which Superstars will be the next to ask for a release, walk away when their contract expires, or retire from the business.

Here are the WWE Superstars who could exit the company in the coming months.

Early Predictions for WrestleMania 43 Match Card 🔮

Nikki Bella may not be an obvious candidate to leave WWE anytime soon, especially since she and Brie Bella recently revealed their new deals run through March 2028 .

However, Bella is 42 years old and has a history of injuries that makes it a real possibility that she doesn't make it through the end of her deal. Nikki and her sister Brie have walked away from WWE to pursue other opportunities in the past, and possible injuries could force them to consider outside opportunities again.

Bella has been open about how her priorities have changed, and her future is more closely tied to retirement than simply becoming a free agent. If she decides one last run isn't possible or doesn't meet her creative standards, her departure would become a major story regardless of when it happens.

While Bella would be a bigger mainstream departure, Johnny Gargano is a much more immediate candidate since his WWE contract situation has already generated legitimate speculation.

According to Yahoo Sports , Gargano has not signed a new WWE contract and is currently set to become a free agent when his existing deal expires. The situation became even more interesting after Gargano returned to the ring in Cleveland and challenged CM Punk for the Undisputed WWE Championship.

Gargano has not publicly confirmed that he is leaving WWE, but the combination of his contract status, recent storyline, and comments about making significant career decisions makes him one of the most intriguing names to watch.

Dragon Lee might be the most fascinating name on this list because his WWE future has suddenly become a legitimate question, even though he has been featured prominently on television.

According to Bryan Alvarez , rumors indicate that Lee's WWE contract is nearing its expiration, while his brother Dralistico's AEW contract is also reportedly coming due soon.

The brothers have trademarked the name "Hermanos Lee," creating an obvious source of speculation about whether they could eventually work together under that name.

Lee has received meaningful opportunities recently, including an Intercontinental Championship match against Chad Gable, but his contract situation and the new trademark make his future worth monitoring.

articles.title: Blockbuster Trade Ideas for Connor McDavid if Oilers Fall Out of Contention During 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Players like Connor McDavid do not get traded.
articles.body:
Players like Connor McDavid do not get traded.

Players like him come along once every couple of decades (or less, depending on where you already put him among the NHL's all-time greats), and if you are lucky enough to get a player like that on your team, you typically do everything in your power to keep them for their entire career.

It is because of that reality that is almost certain that McDavid is not going to get traded away from the Edmonton Oilers anytime soon. Probably not ever.

The key words there are "almost certain" and "probably."

Nothing is ever fully guaranteed. Nothing is ever 100 percent. And Oilers fans have to know that as well as anyone given that the NHL's actual GOAT, Wayne Gretzky, did in fact get traded away from this organization at one point in his career.

Whether they are willing to admit it or not, there also has to be at least some concern from Oilers fans, and perhaps even the Oilers themselves, that McDavid could become frustrated if the team underachieves and again fall short of Stanley Cup contender status.

When it came time to sign his most recent contract extension, he only opted for a short-term, two-year deal that essentially resulted in him taking a massive pay cut in terms of salary cap percentage. Some could take that as a message to Oilers management that it's time to get serious about building around him. That's probably how it should have been taken. It might also explain some of the desperation moves the team has made ever since.

There is also a growing trend, especially this offseason, of some of the league's star players forcing their way out of situations they are not happy in or do not feel they can win in. While it did not come from an official request, Vancouver traded Quinn Hughes because they knew he was not re-signing there. Minnesota might have to soon wrestle with a similar decision regarding him. Brady Tkachuk forced his way out of Ottawa. Dylan Larkin is trying to force his way out of Detroit. Connor Hellebuyck is so committed to getting out of Winnipeg that he didn't even show up to training camp and is taking a suspension from the team. The common denominator with that quartet of players is they were all teammates on Team USA at the 2026 Olympics, and McDavid, as a Canadian player, is not within that inner circle. Maybe that's a part of it for them.

But he is still going to be 30 years old this season, in his 12th year in the NHL, and is still searching for a Stanley Cup ring. Until he gets it, he is going to keep hearing the "yeah, but..." that always follows him around when he is discussed among the game's current and all-time best.

He needs to win at some point, and he knows it. And if he loses faith that it will ever happen for him in Edmonton, you have to at least entertain the "what ifs."

Let's play the "what if" game and just hypothetically envision a scenario where the Oilers fall out of contention this season, and it results in McDavid eventually becoming the latest star player to ask out of their current situation.

The problem with suggesting a Connor McDavid trade

There are actually a few problems, ranging from Edmonton's willingness to ever actually do something like this, to McDavid actually trying to force a move.

Finding a trade partner that would not only entice McDavid (and he would have full control over this given his trade protections in his contracts), but also have the trade assets that would entice Edmonton to even entertain the idea, would be among the biggest of those problems.

Winning a Cup would be McDavid's only motivation, and that automatically limits the potential partners.

But how many contenders would have the pieces to actually pull that off?

It's almost impossible to find comparable value or returns because, again, players of this caliber almost never get traded. You can't even go back to the era of the Gretzky or Eric Lindros trades because the NHL is a completely different world right now. Teams are smarter, player and draft pick values are different, there is a salary cap to contend with and you might as well be comparing apples to bell peppers.

First, let's just ask this question: Who are the best players over the past 10-15 to have actually been traded, and what were the returns on them?

Mikko Rantanen was traded as a pending UFA for Martin Necas, Jack Drury and some draft picks.

Quinn Hughes, with a year-and-a-half remaining on his deal, was traded for a package that included Marco Rossi, Zeev Buium, Liam Ohgren and a first-round pick.

Matthew Tkachuk and Jonathan Huberdeau (who, at the time, was an elite scorer) were traded for each other, with MacKenzie Weegar joining Huberdeau as part of the package going to Calgary.

Brady Tkachuk was traded for three first-round picks.

Jack Eichel was traded for Alex Tuch, Peyton Krebs and multiple draft picks.

Erik Karlsson went from Ottawa to San Jose for a pile of draft picks (including an eventual No. 3 overall pick that was used to select Tim Stutzle), Joshua Norris and some depth roster players.

P.K. Subban and Shea Weber were traded for each other.

Taylor Hall was traded straight up for Adam Larsson.

You are either looking at one established, big-time star going back the other way, or one really good young player, one top prospect, and a bunch of draft pick capital.

Even that is difficult because for as great as those players all are, McDavid is still probably a tier above them just based on status, star-power and offensive production.

Is there a contending team that could get into that ballpark, or exceed it?

There are not many of them that hit the sweet spot of being good enough to make a play for it and also having the right trade pieces to offer.

Florida and Vegas are in on every star play, and most star players want to go to both places, but their trade options and assets are very limited.

There are a lot of teams that would have a bounty of young trade assets (San Jose, Chicago, Anaheim) but still have a long way to go before they become true contenders.

Toronto and New York are big markets, but where do those teams see themselves in the coming years? And again it comes down to interesting trade assets. Do either of them have it?

Would they move him to a Western Conference team like Dallas or Minnesota?

These are all big questions and hurdles.

It's these factors, more than anything, that might make this an unrealistic scenario, and even if McDavid did eventually frustrated and want out, it might just be a situation that ends up going to free agency, or a last-minute trade deadline move next year if things really go south on (and off) the ice.

There's also the very likely scenario where Edmonton is still good, and still a contender, rendering a discussion like this completely meaningless.

But there are three teams that might hit the sweet spot that would be needed here should it ever come to something like this.

We have talked for years about how the one big weakness for this era of Carolina hockey has been the lack of a true, game-changing superstar. That's not meant to be a knock on the roster or their top players. They are a lot of outstanding players here, and have been for quite some time. But it's always been a team built on depth, system, and a roster where the whole is always greater than the sum of its parts. There was a thought that until they found a true top-tier superstar that it was going to be tough for them to break through and win it all (and they took a big swing for that superstar in trying to add Rantanen).

In 2025-26, they finally put that talk to bed and ended up breaking through and winning the Cup without the true "superstar."

Maybe the rest of the team is good enough as is (and it obviously is).

But Carolina would still be an intriguing option because A) it's a championship-caliber team, and B) it has the type of assets and draft pick capital throughout the organization that could probably get a deal of this magnitude completed.

The idea: Seth Jarvis, K'Andre Miller and a first-round pick to Edmonton

It's the same basic structure as the Tkachuk-Huberdeau trade where a top-line forward and a top-pairing defenseman are the focal point going back. It's also arguably a better package (as it would need to be) because Jarvis is younger and cheaper than Huberdeau was for Calgary, and is likely to keep getting better for another couple of years instead of immediately going in the tank the way Huberdeau did. It also works in the short-term because Jarvis is the type of player that would be the centerpiece of such a deal and also has no trade limitations in his contract at the moment.

I don't know if Buffalo is going to end up being a serious Stanley Cup contender in the coming seasons, but you do not have to squint too hard to see the potential for it. They finally got through to the playoffs in 2025-26 after 14 years away, and even won a round. It's a good young team, with a lot of talent.

I think I just like the idea of suggesting Buffalo because everybody in Buffalo thought they were going to originally get him back in 2014, they ended up with Jack Eichel instead, and that entire thing just collapsed on itself and never worked out for anybody.

Buffalo also has some potential pieces that could make something work.

Plus, McDavid has some familiarity with the area having played his junior hockey about 90 minutes away in Erie, Pennsylvania.

The idea: Tage Thompson, Mattias Samuelsson and a first-round pick to Edmonton

Again, it's a star player that isn't quite on the superstar level (Thompson) and a very good defensive player in Samuelsson. Samuelsson has been a big part of the Sabres blue line, but they would still have Rasmus Dahlin and Owen Power, while some of the team's best prospects, including 2026 No. 4 overall pick Daxon Rudolph, play defense. So there is something of a pipeline there that could make a player like Samuelsson expendable in a situation like this.

Buffalo has good reason to like the core it is building, and Thompson has been a big part of turning things around, but is he the type of player that is the best player on a serious Stanley Cup contender? And would McDavid see Buffalo as a Stanley Cup contender to go there?

The Lightning are still on that contender level, but they strike me as a contender that has grown stale.

It's still a very good team. But it's a very good team that has not won a playoff series in four years.

It is also a team that is not afraid to make bold changes and take big swings.

Nikita Kucherov is sitting out there as an unrestricted free agent after this season with no contract in place. They have said goodbye to franchise icons in the past, and I would not put it past them to do it again. Especially if it coincided with another blockbuster move that could change the dynamic of the team a little bit.

The idea: Brayden Point, Erik Cernak and a first-round pick to Edmonton

Point's no-movement clause and whether or not he would waive it for Edmonton would be a big potential obstacle for this idea, but the value seems solid. He's a similar age to McDavid, still has years of term left on his deal and is still an All-Star level forward.

articles.title: 6 Early Trade Landing Spots for Pavel Zacha Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: The Boston Bruins' struggles last fall sparked trade speculation about Pavel Zacha, who'd been a fixture in the rumor mill during the summer of 2025.
articles.body:
The Boston Bruins' struggles last fall sparked trade speculation about Pavel Zacha, who'd been a fixture in the rumor mill during the summer of 2025.

After missing the 2025 playoffs, the retooling Bruins were expected to be sellers in the trade market if they continued to stumble in 2025-26, with Zacha a prime trade chip. By November, the rumors reached the point where we listed possible landing spots for the talented two-way center.

However, the Bruins overcame their early difficulties and clinched a wild-card berth with 100 points. Zacha played a key role, netting a career-high 30 goals and 65 points.

Zacha is in the final season of a four-year contract with an average annual value of $4.8 million. He also has an eight-team no-trade list and is eligible for unrestricted free agent status next July.

On Sept. 15, Steve Conroy of the Boston Herald reported that it remained uncertain whether Zacha would get a contract extension. Shortly afterward, general manager Don Sweeney stated that talks between the two sides were ongoing and that he had had good dialogue with the center's agent.

Zacha will start this season in Boston. However, playoff contenders will monitor his contract status, especially if the Bruins are out of the postseason race by the March 1 trade deadline. Here are six teams that could be in the market for a center like Zacha.

After 14 long seasons, the Buffalo Sabres ended their record-setting playoff drought by topping the Atlantic Division last season. After coming within a Game 7 overtime goal of reaching the Eastern Conference Final, they're hungry to build on last season's promising performance.

Tage Thompson could remain their first-line center , but played on the wing at times last season and could again if Josh Norris centers that line. However, Norris has an injury history, and the Sabres might need another seasoned center if Norris is sidelined again.

Pavel Zacha could be an attractive rental option for the Sabres if younger options like Noah Östlund, Jiri Kulich, or Konsta Helenius aren't ready for the role. His experience could be as invaluable to the Sabres as his versatility and two-way skills.

The Sabres have plenty of promising youngsters on their roster and within their system to make an enticing offer to the Bruins. If they're only interested in Zacha as a rental, they could instead pitch a couple of draft picks, including a first-rounder, depending on what other clubs are offering.

The retirement of former captain Anze Kopitar leaves a void at center on the Los Angeles Kings' top two lines. Quinton Byfield is expected to fill the first-line role, with Erik Haula and Scott Laughton as middle-six centers. Daily Faceoff has winger Adrian Kempe pencilled into the first-line role .

If Byfield or Kempe struggles on the first line, or if Haula and Laughton can't suitably fill the second-line role, the Kings could be in the market for a center, with Pavel Zacha as an attractive trade target if available.

Zacha's two-way skills would make him a solid short-term option as the Kings' first-line center. If Byfield is fulfilling that role, Zacha could easily fill the second-line position, where he's best suited.

It could cost the Kings a first-round pick and one of their top prospects to acquire Zacha as a playoff rental if he's on pace for another 30-goal, 60-point season. If they hope to re-sign Zacha, the asking price could include a young roster player.

It's no secret that the Minnesota Wild were in the market for a centerman this summer. Trade rumors linked them to Dylan Larkin after it was reported that the Detroit Red Wings center requested a trade . The Wild were reportedly on his three-team trade list.

However, the Wild weren't willing to part with winger Matt Boldy for Larkin. Unless that asking price changes, they'll have to consider other options, such as Pavel Zacha.

The Wild are currently using the versatile Ryan Hartman as their first-line center , but he's more suited as a middle-six winger. They need an elite first-line center to skate between Boldy and Kirill Kaprizov, but Zacha would be a good upgrade as a playoff rental, and they could re-sign him if he performs well.

After parting with three young players acquiring Quinn Hughes last season, the Wild are a little thin on prospects . The Bruins' asking price could include promising center Charlie Stramel or a young forward like Danila Yurov.

Trades between the Boston Bruins and Montréal Canadiens are rare given the long-time rivalry between these Original Six franchises. However, it's not out of the question for the Canadiens to land Zacha if the Bruins are out of playoff contention by the March 1 trade deadline.

The Canadiens are a rising force in the Eastern Conference. NHL.com's Dan Rosen has them atop his list of this season's Stanley Cup contenders . However, they lack an experienced two-way center to skate on their second line between young stars Ivan Demikov and Juraj Slafkovský.

On June 18, Arpon Basu of The Athletic suggested Zacha as a great fit to center the Canadiens' second line. However, his UFA eligibility next July could limit what they would offer the Bruins in a trade. He also suggested another hurdle would be what Zacha would want on his next contract.

Still, Montréal could make a pitch if Zacha becomes available. The Canadiens could part with a first-rounder as part of the return if he's willing to sign a reasonable extension. They can also draw on their considerable depth of promising young roster players and prospects for trade bait.

On June 2, the Nashville Predators hired Chris MacFarland as their new president of hockey operations and general manager. The former GM of the Colorado Avalanche has been busy in the trade market , attempting to retool the Predators' roster.

MacFarland could be looking for a center for his top two lines this season, especially if the Predators are in the postseason hunt by the March 1 trade deadline. They will need a potential replacement for 36-year-old Ryan O'Reilly, who is UFA-eligible on July 1.

Having already acquired promising Mavrik Bourque in June, MacFarland could make a pitch for Pavel Zacha. He would be a reasonable short-term option to replace O'Reilly until a more suitable first-line center is found

The Predators have plenty of extra draft picks to use as trade capital, including a conditional 2028 first-round pick from the Colorado Avalanche. Depending on the Bruins' asking price, they could also add a prospect like David Edstrom or Reid Schaefer.

Despite barely making the playoffs last season, the Vegas Golden Knights surprised experts by reaching the Stanley Cup Final, including an impressive sweep of the Presidents' Trophy-winning Colorado Avalanche in the Western Conference Final.

However, center William Karlsson's wrist injury in Game 5 of the Stanley Cup Final contributed to their series loss to the Carolina Hurricanes. Given the 33-year-old Karlsson's injury history, the ever-opportunistic Golden Knights could pursue an experienced top-six center like Pavel Zacha.

Zacha could comfortably fill that second-line center role for the Golden Knights. He could also drop into the third-line role if Tomas Hertl were moved up, or move to the wing if necessary.

Salary cap space and limited trade capital could make it difficult for the Golden Knights to outbid other teams for Zacha. Nevertheless, we cannot dismiss their creativity in finding ways to land players they want by the trade deadline.
