articles.title: WWE's Bizarre Oba Femi Plan, Penta Stays Red-Hot, A New Star Emerges and more Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The September 21 edition of Raw on Netflix from the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas featured shocking moments and two Money in the Bank qualifiers.
articles.body:
The September 21 edition of Raw on Netflix from the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas featured shocking moments and two Money in the Bank qualifiers.

Roxanne Perez defeated Iyo Sky and La Catalina to qualify for the women's MITB. Meanwhile, 946 attacked and abducted Solo Sikoa, costing him his ladder match qualifier.

Penta stepped up in Sikoa's place and qualified for the ladder match over Dominik Mysterio and Dragon Lee. Stephanie Vaquer also announced she would fight both Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch for the Women's World Championship soon.

For all the immediate fallout from this eventful show, scroll down.

Penta on Track to Be World Champion in the Next Year

Since Penta's show-stopping performance against Roman Reigns last week, the luchador has been the talk of WWE.

It was easy to question what was next after he was so close to capture the World Heavyweight Championship. The answer was Money in the Bank.

The luchador enters the men's Money in the Bank ladder match with the most momentum, and that is typically a good sign of the eventual winner.

While Bron Breakker or Trick Williams could also make sense, Penta is the one man in this field that feels destined to be world champion in the next year.

Even without MITB, Penta's name should be lined up for 2027, possibly even getting that win as early as WrestleMania 43.

Roxanne Perez is New Women's Money in the Bank Favorite

While Roxanne Perez was not the favorite going into a triple threat qualifier that also featured Iyo Sky, her victory sets her up as the new favorite to win the ladder match.

Sol Ruca, Lola Vice and Jacy Jayne all feel too fresh to be on track for a world title run. The Prodigy though has waited her turn and played her role well to date.

As the forgotten woman in The Judgment Day, she could instantly become a threat by winning Money in the Bank, creating a constant problem for even her own stablemate Liv Morgan.

The win could be the catalyst for change in The Judgment Day where Perez is able to take the Women's World Championship instead of Liv. Perhaps WWE would even set up The Prodigy to cash in on Liv after she reclaims the gold.

No matter what, Perez as Mrs. MITB is too good a story to pass up. The 24-year-old star would instantly become one of WWE's most important women for the next decade.

La Catalina on the Fast Track to Main Roster Success

The new AAA Reina de Reinas champion is already working Raw and not in Mexico. The Chilean star was positioned as a star-in-the-making in Texas.

That rise up the ranks should continue for Catalina, who is a star in look and performance.

While she is necessary to AAA's limited women's division, Raw is also limited on women and could bring Catalina in regularly as a credible threat to anyone.

This also gives AAA another recognizable face to the larger WWE Universe, positioning her as a must-watch star.

WWE should consider bringing in more women from AAA on occasion, especially Las Tóxicas as more stars to freshen up the women's division.

Early Predictions for WrestleMania 43 Match Card 🔮

Becky Lynch Should Never Be a Heel Ever Again

The latest heel run for Becky Lynch went as usual for The Man. She found success while trying her best to elevate the talent around her.

However, Lynch was never the top star that WWE needed, and that has quickly changed with her return to a babyface role.

The crowd wants to embrace and elevate The Man, and her natural charm on the microphone is more suited to a crowd-favorable reaction.

At 39 years old, Lynch is older than many women that have already retired in WWE, but she is still obviously working at her best on the mic and in the ring.

Even if she chooses to work well into her 40s, The Man should not return to a heel role again. This is the perfect veteran face to work off anyone in the women's division.

WWE needs her star power maximized in order to highlight the next generation that want to reach for her enduring level of success.

WWE is delaying the inevitable crowning of Oba Femi as a world champion. His immediate problem is The Vision.

It now looks like The Ruler has some help in the form of Je'Von Evans, a fellow NXT call-up that he has faced many times in the ring.

All indications are that Oba and Je'Von will work together against The Vision, and that should include going after the World Tag Team Championships.

These two were the generational rivalry of their NXT era and should also have strong chemistry as teammates.

While this will work for the short term, it does clearly show that WWE is simply delaying the inevitable.

Both Oba and Je'Von could be singles champions and likely will be in the future, but much like Cody Rhodes between WrestleMania 39 and 40, The Ruler could go on a tag team side question simply to pass the time.

articles.title: 10 Sports Dream Teams That Turned Into Nightmares
articles.summary: Building a championship team in professional sports is not always as easy as just stacking a bunch of high-profile talent onto one roster and turning them loose on their respective league.
articles.body:
Building a championship team in professional sports is not always as easy as just stacking a bunch of high-profile talent onto one roster and turning them loose on their respective league.

For every "Big Three" that has worked in the NBA, there are far more examples of the idea failing miserably. For every offseason spending spree that led to a World Series title, there have been significantly more high-priced flops.

Here, we've ranked the 10 most significant examples of dream teams that turned into nightmares, spanning everything from the four major sports to the Olympics, soccer and golf. They're ranked by how far they fell short of expectations.

For anyone who was a fan of these teams, apologies in advance for reopening old wounds.

The Rockets brought together Scottie Pippen, Charles Barkley and Hakeem Olajuwon in an effort to seize control of the NBA in a post-Michael Jordan world. They finished 31-19, but they were bumped in the first round of the playoffs, and Pippen was sent to Portland that offseason after feuding with Barkley.

In his first offseason in the general manager's seat, A.J. Preller gutted the Padres farm system and brought aboard Matt Kemp, Justin Upton, James Shields, Craig Kimbrel and Wil Myers. They ended up winning three fewer games than they had the previous season, finishing 74-88.

In the summer of 2021, a PSG roster that already featured Neymar and Kylian Mbappé added Lionel Messi. While they were dominant domestically, they suffered back-to-back Round of 16 exits in the Champions League, leading to the eventual departure of Neymar and Messi.

With a record-setting $331 million Opening Day payroll, anchored by co-aces Justin Verlander and Max Scherzer who were making $43.3 million apiece, the Mets were all-in under owner Steve Cohen. By August, they had traded away Verlander and Scherzer on their way to a 75-87 finish and a luxury-tax bill north of $100 million.

Just days after Mat Ishbia was announced as the new owner of the Phoenix Suns, the organization swung a blockbuster trade to acquire Kevin Durant from the Brooklyn Nets in exchange for Mikal Bridges, Cam Johnson, Jae Crowder, four first-round picks and a pick swap.

Later that offseason, the Suns acquired three-time All-Star Bradley Beal from the Washington Wizards in exchange for Chris Paul, Landry Shamet and multiple first-round pick swaps and second-round picks. With that duo joining incumbent star Devin Booker, the Suns suddenly had a "Big Three."

Various injuries kept the trio from building any sort of real chemistry during the 2023-24 season, with Beal in particular limited to 53 games. But the bigger issue was a glaring lack of a true point guard on the roster.

The Suns went 49-33 to claim the No. 6 seed in the West, but the Minnesota Timberwolves swept them in the first round. That led to the dismissal of head coach Frank Vogel, although things went from bad to worse under Mike Budenholzer the following year, and they missed the postseason entirely.

The Suns traded Durant and waive-and-stretched Beal following the 2024-25 season, and a team led by Booker and Dillon Brooks went 45-37 and returned to the playoffs last year.

After the Washington Commanders finished 10-6 and won the NFC East title in 1999, second-year owner Daniel Snyder went on an offseason spending spree. He added cornerback Deion Sanders (seven years, $56 million), defensive end Bruce Smith (five years, $23 million), safety Mark Carrier (five years, $15.9 million) and quarterback Jeff George (four years, $18.25 million) to a roster that already featured star running back Stephen Davis and Hall of Fame cornerback Champ Bailey.

The Commanders also held the No. 2 and No. 3 overall picks in the 2000 NFL draft, which they used to select linebacker LaVar Arrington and offensive tackle Chris Samuels. That was enough to put them on the short list of Super Bowl favorites (+350) to start the season.

After a 6-2 start, the Commanders lost six of their next seven games. The star-studded locker room fractured, and Snyder overstepped as owner, meddling in a quarterback controversy between George and Brad Johnson.

Head coach Norv Turner was abruptly fired with three games left in the season, and the Commanders finished 8-8, missing the postseason entirely.

Sanders retired after one season of his seven-year deal, and Johnson left Washington and immediately won a Super Bowl in Tampa Bay. Meanwhile, the financial ramifications of the spending spree hindered the Commanders for years.

In search of their first playoff appearance since the 1996-97 season, the New York Rangers front office piled up talent ahead of the 2001-02 and 2002-03 seasons. They traded for Eric Lindros and Pavel Bure and signed Bobby Holik to a massive five-year, $45 million contract.

During that stretch, the roster also featured captain Mark Messier, winger Theoren Fleury, defenseman Brian Leetch and goalie Mike Richter, giving them no shortage of star power and legitimate Stanley Cup aspirations.

Injuries and a general lack of chemistry among their aging stars led to a 36-38-4-4 record in 2001-02, leaving the Rangers out of the playoffs for a fifth straight year.

General manager Glen Sather took over as head coach midway through the 2002-03 season to try to right the ship, but an $80 million roster could only produce a 32-36-10-4 record.

Their playoff drought ultimately stretched to seven years before the 2004-05 lockout forced a hard reset.

After a disappointing 77-84 finish in 1991 that was preceded by seven straight winning seasons, the New York Mets entered the offseason looking for a quick fix and attempted to throw money at the problem.

They signed Bobby Bonilla (five years, $29 million) and Eddie Murray (two years, $7.5 million) in free agency, re-signed John Franco (two years, $8 million) and traded for former Cy Young winner Bret Saberhagen, adding them to a roster led by Dwight Gooden, David Cone and Howard Johnson.

The Mets were 29-28 on June 9. That was the last day in the 1992 season that they were above .500.

The locker room was a dumpster fire, Saberhagen missed time due to injuries, Cone was traded to Toronto, and Johnson went from leading the NL in home runs (38) and RBI (117) in 1991 to a 91 OPS+ and negative-1.4 WAR in 1992.

The Mets finished 72-90, a whopping 24 games out of first place in the NL East. What was a three-year playoff drought heading into the 1992 season ended up stretching to 1999, partly because of the aftermath of their spending.

Looking to maximize the final few years of Kobe Bryant's prime, the Lakers swung a pair of blockbuster deals to acquire Steve Nash and Dwight Howard prior to the 2012-13 season.

It cost significant draft capital and young center Andrew Bynum to get those deals done, but they made the Lakers instant title front-runners as that duo joined Bryant, Pau Gasol and Metta World Peace.

Firing your head coach five games into the season generally isn't a good sign for a smooth season ahead. The Lakers showed Mike Brown the door after a 1-4 start, and his replacement, Mike D'Antoni, inherited a team that didn't fit his fast-paced style.

Nash suffered a fractured fibula in the second game of the season that cost him almost two months, Gasol played 49 games while navigating a torn plantar fascia, Howard played through a torn labrum, and Bryant eventually suffered a torn Achilles tendon in April.

The Lakers finished 45-37 before getting swept in the first round of the playoffs by the San Antonio Spurs. The ill-fated experiment ended that offseason when Howard walked in free agency.

With a high-powered offense led by Michael Vick, LeSean McCoy and DeSean Jackson and a 10-win season in 2010, the Philadelphia Eagles set to work building a defense to match during the 2011 offseason.

They signed cornerback Nnamdi Asomugha (five years, $60 million), edge-rusher Jason Babin (five years, $28.9 million) and defensive tackle Cullen Jenkins (five years, $30.4 million) in free agency, while they traded for Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie to give themselves a potentially elite cornerback tandem.

During training camp, backup quarterback Vince Young called the Eagles a "Dream Team." The hype train flew out of the station and straight into a brick wall as the Eagles got off to a 1-4 start.

The questionable decision to move longtime offensive line coach Juan Castillo to defensive coordinator flopped. His zone coverage scheme was an especially poor fit for Asomugha, who had thrived in press/man coverage in Oakland.

Three of the Eagles' early losses came from fourth-quarter collapses, and they never recovered, finishing 8-8 and missing the playoffs. The following year, they went 4-12 and fired head coach Andy Reid after the season.

The 1992, 1996 and 2000 U.S. Olympic basketball teams went a combined 24-0 while outscoring the opposition by more than 750 points. But a sixth-place finish at the 2002 FIBA World Championship left them with something to prove heading into the 2004 Olympics.

With Tim Duncan and Allen Iverson serving as team captains, the young trio of LeBron James, Carmelo Anthony and Dwyane Wade injected some youth and excitement into a roster expected to claim gold once again. Stephon Marbury, Shawn Marion and Lamar Odom were also key contributors.

A lack of knockdown outside shooting and a roster poorly constructed for the FIBA style of play left Team USA exposed. A 92-73 loss to Puerto Rico in the group-play opener marked the first time a U.S. team made up of NBA players had lost a game at the Olympics.

They finished 3-2 in group play, also falling to Lithuania, before knocking off Spain to reach the semifinals. Despite the surprising stumbles, they were still in a position to potentially win gold.

That dream ended with an 89-81 loss to Manu Ginóbili and Argentina, but they at least won a bronze medal by avenging their earlier loss to Lithuania. The "Redeem Team" reclaimed the narrative of dominance four years later, and the U.S. has not surrendered gold since.

Let's just list them off: Tiger Woods, Phil Mickelson, Dustin Johnson, Jordan Spieth, Justin Thomas, Bubba Watson, Rickie Fowler, Bryson DeChambeau, Brooks Koepka, Webb Simpson, Patrick Reed and Tony Finau.

Nine major champions with a combined 31 major titles, and what looked on paper like the greatest collection of golfing talent ever assembled for the Ryder Cup.

After the U.S. got off to 3-1 start on Friday morning, things quickly began to go south. The Americans were swept in the afternoon, marking Europe's first foursomes sweep in Ryder Cup history.

The U.S. trailed 10-6 heading into Sunday, and after showing some brief signs of life, ultimately lost 17.5-10.5 in the most lopsided Ryder Cup result since 2006.

Woods (0-4), Mickelson (0-2) and DeChambeau (0-3) went a combined 0-9 while serving as three of Jim Furyk's four captain picks.

Real Madrid club president Florentino Pérez made it a focal point to sign one global superstar deemed a "Galáctico" every summer while trying to build an international juggernaut.

By 2003, he already had a roster that featured Zinedine Zidane, Luis Figo, Ronaldo and Raúl when he signed David Beckham from Manchester United to complete the star-studded team.

Despite all the high-priced talent, Real Madrid went three straight seasons without winning La Liga, the Copa del Rey or the Champions League.

The top-heavy roster eventually faltered due to its defensive shortcomings, and the decision to sell midfielder Claude Makélélé to Chelsea left a glaring hole on the defensive side of things.

Pérez resigned in February 2006, effectively bringing the original Galácticos experiment to an end, and the roster was dismantled from there.

The Brooklyn Nets signed Kevin Durant and Kyrie Irving as free agents in 2019. But with Durant recovering from the ruptured right Achilles tendon that he suffered during the NBA Finals the previous season and Irving limited to 20 games due to shoulder surgery, their first season together was a wash.

Prior to the 2020-21 season, the Nets hired Steve Nash as their new head coach. And in January, they added a third superstar to the mix by acquiring James Harden from the Houston Rockets for a blockbuster package of players and picks.

The Nets advanced to the second round of the 2021 NBA playoffs, but Harden suffered a hamstring strain in Game 1, Irving sprained his ankle in Game 4, and they fell in seven games to the Bucks when a potential game-winning three-pointer from Durant in Game 7 was ruled a two with his toe on the line.

The following year, Irving was unable to play home games due to New York City's COVID-19 vaccine mandate, and Harden eventually requested a trade. He landed in Philadelphia in exchange for Ben Simmons, who wound up missing the rest of the season because of a back injury. The Nets still won 44 games, but were swept in the first round by the Boston Celtics.

Then it all came to an end during the 2022-23 season, as Nash was fired seven games into the season before Irving (to Dallas) and Durant (to Phoenix) were both traded in February.

All told, the "Big Three" of Durant, Irving and Harden played a grand total of 16 games together.

articles.title: 6-year-old girl sets Rubik's Cube speed record, Chinese state media say
articles.summary: Lian Yunzhi, who practices 2 to 3 hours daily, has become the first female speedcuber to average under 4.5 seconds in competition, according to Chinese state...
articles.body:
A 6-year-old Chinese girl has set a new women's world record for solving a 3x3 Rubik's Cube in just over 4 seconds, state media reported Tuesday.

Young speedcuber Lian Yunzhi broke the women's 3x3 average world record twice in three days at two World Cube Association certified competitions in Wuhan and Guangzhou, according to state broadcaster CCTV on Monday.

She posted averages of 4.52 and 4.27 seconds after solving the Rubik's Cube five times.

Lian, who is from Chengdu, in China's southern Sichuan province, is "the first female speedcuber to average under 4.5 seconds," CCTV added.

A video CCTV posted showed the small girl wearing a red gingham bow on her head as she deftly turned and twisted a Rubik's Cube.

After solving the puzzle, she placed the cube on the table, clapped her hands and fist pumped the air.

Nicknamed "Zhizhi," Lian was first introduced to the Rubik's Cube after being enrolled into a class as a child — one of various extracurriculars alongside dance and music lessons, her mother Lin Yangxi told local media outlets, according to the AFP news agency.

Lin "gradually realized" that cubing was an "excellent activity for fostering a child's comprehensive abilities" and shifted her focus toward it, she told Chengdu's Red Star News.

Her daughter has now mastered over 1,300 Rubik's Cube solving algorithms, practicing daily for 2 to 3 hours, Lin said.

Photos from Red Star News showed Lian's trophies displayed on a shelf in her home.

"Solving a Rubik's Cube improves focus, memory, logical thinking, spatial awareness, and helps develop a healthy mindset toward winning and losing," Lin said.

"It's not just about blindly memorizing formulas, but using logical reasoning to find optimal solutions," she added.

articles.title: For PWHL San Jose, There Is No Question More Pressing Than Where Will Their Goals Come From?
articles.summary: San Jose has plenty of speed and upside up front, but Troy Ryan is counting on several players to take the next step offensively.
articles.body:
The question surrounding PWHL San Jose 's forwards isn't complicated: Who is going to score?

That might be the biggest question facing Troy Ryan's roster heading into its first season. San Jose has speed, versatility and plenty of international experience, but it doesn't have the established offensive star that some of the other expansion teams were able to add. There isn't an obvious 20-goal scorer sitting at the top of the lineup.

That doesn't mean the forward group is without options. In fact, there are plenty of reasons to think it could be better than it looks on paper.

There are just as many reasons to wonder how quickly that happens.

Ryan knows what he's getting from Kristin O'Neill and Maggie Connors.

O'Neill was San Jose's Expansion Foundational Offer player, giving the team a center with three seasons of PWHL experience who can be trusted in a variety of situations. She also spent part of last season with Canada's Olympic team and won a silver medal at the 2026 Winter Olympics.

Connors followed Ryan from Toronto to San Jose on a two-year contract after playing all three of her PWHL seasons under him.

Neither has put up big offensive numbers at this level. O'Neill had five points in 30 games with the New York Sirens last season, while Connors finished with the same total in Toronto. But Ryan isn't bringing them in because he expects either player to suddenly become a top-line scorer.

He's bringing them in because he knows what they can do, and because they give him a foundation to build around, while looking towards the future with his younger forwards.

Anne Cherkowski and Maddi Wheeler both spent last season with the Sirens, and neither had a breakout year. Cherkowski has the speed to create chances when she gets space, while Wheeler is still early enough in her professional career that there's room for her game to develop.

Reichen Kirchmaier discusses joining PWHL San Jose

Natálie Mlýnková may have the clearest opportunity of the group.

She joined San Jose after winning the Walter Cup with Montreal and finished her rookie season with 10 points. She has also represented Czechia at two Olympics and was named Hockey East Player of the Year in 2024.

Montreal had a deep forward group. San Jose doesn't, at least not yet. That should give Mlýnková more opportunity to play and potentially take on a bigger offensive role.

If she makes that jump, it changes the outlook considerably.

Laila Edwards could also become part of that equation, even if her position remains somewhat fluid. San Jose selected her fourth overall in June after she won Olympic gold with the United States. Ryan has already talked about the possibility of using her at forward and on the back end of the power play.

The problem is that much of that upside is still hypothetical.

O'Neill and Connors have experience, but neither has been a major offensive producer in the PWHL. Mlýnková showed promise in her first season, but 10 points isn't enough to assume she'll suddenly become one of the league's top scorers. Cherkowski and Wheeler are still trying to establish themselves.

And while Edwards could become a major offensive piece, San Jose can't reasonably expect their rookie to carry an expansion team's scoring from the moment she arrives.

That leaves Ryan relying on several players to take a step at roughly the same time.

That's not necessarily a bad strategy. Expansion teams rarely get to build a perfect roster in their first year, and there is value in having players who still have room to grow… but it does make San Jose difficult to project.

The Hockey News gave San Jose's 2026 draft class an A, pointing to the two-way ability and upside the team added beyond Edwards. Sloane Matthews, Lily Shannon, McKenna Van Gelder and Reichen Kirchmair give the organization more young forwards to develop.

They aren't expected to solve the scoring problem immediately and that's probably a good thing, because asking a group of rookies to do so would be unrealistic.

This is where the roster construction gets interesting.

San Jose doesn't appear to have one player who will be responsible for carrying the offense. It will probably need contributions from several lines, with players taking on larger roles than they have had previously.

Maybe Mlýnková becomes a bigger offensive threat. Maybe Cherkowski's speed translates into more production. Maybe Wheeler takes a significant step. Maybe Edwards immediately looks like the kind of player capable of driving offense at this level.

Ryan doesn't need every one of those things to happen.

That is the gamble with this group. There is a lot to like about the players individually, but there isn't much proven scoring among them. The upside is real; so is the uncertainty.

That's what makes this forward group so interesting heading into the season. There are plenty of players Ryan can reasonably expect to contribute, and several who could be better than their previous numbers suggest.

What San Jose doesn't have yet is certainty.

The blue line looks like the more settled part of the roster. Up front, Ryan has more questions, more room for development and fewer guarantees.

For an expansion team, that can work. It just means someone has to take the next step.

articles.title: Aaron Donald feels the love and soreness after first game back with Rams
articles.summary: Aaron Donald recorded three tackles, including one that resulted in a loss, in the Rams’ 28-6 victory over the Giants at SoFi Stadium.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — Aaron Donald wore the biggest smile after the Los Angeles Rams' 28-6 victory over the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on Monday, Sept. 21.

Donald made his way out of the tunnel during pregame player introductions to a loud cheer from the stadium crowd, which included members of his family.

The defensive tackle produced three tackles, including one that resulted in a loss.

"I felt the love after I had that tackle for a loss and they were cheering for me," Donald said.

The tackle tied Donald with Lavonte David and Von Miller (177) for fourth on the all-time tackles for loss list.

Can't-miss alternate and throwback uniforms of the 2026 NFL season

J.J. Watt is third on the list with 195 tackles, with Calais Campbell (196) in second and Terrell Suggs (202) in first. The NFL officially began holding the record for most career tackles for a loss since 1999.

Donald spent time amongst the fans after his postgame press conference, shaking hands and signing some autographs as fans continued to cheer for him.

One of Donald's biggest takeaways was the need to work on his timing moving forward, admitting he could've worked faster to win his 1-on-1 matchups.

"I'm a little sore right now," Donald said. "But it feels good to be back out there and get that first game under my belt. … I'm officially back playing football."

Donald did appear to have a wrap around his right hand during the press conference. When asked about it directly, he again just chalked it up to being sore and playing after just two padded practices.

Coach Sean McVay was thrilled to have one of his starting defenders back on the field and the impact he made beyond the stat sheet.

"His overall energy," McVay said, talking about Donald's impact on the team. "One of the things is he elicits attention. He brings everybody up around him and I didn't think it was by coincidence that was the energy that we played with.

"... I thought the defensive coaches did a great job of their game plan, but ultimately just elevating situations he's in and people that he's around. That's what the greats do and that's what he does."

Donald and the Rams will be back in action against the Denver Broncos in a nonconference road game on Sunday, Sept, 27.

articles.title: Is Ageu finally ready to prove his worth?
articles.summary: Wouter Vrancken has transformed the style of play within months, guided Hearts into the Conference League and the League Cup semi-finals.  It has reached the...
articles.body:
Despite defeat at Falkirk and a draw at Kilmarnock heading into the extended international break, the bigger picture for Hearts looks encouraging.

A quick Tynecastle health check suggests the patient is in decent shape. Wouter Vrancken has transformed the style of play within months, guided Hearts into the Conference League and the League Cup semi-finals.

With a realistic chance of lifting that trophy for the first time in 63 years, there is far more to savour than sulk about.

We sit third, which is roughly where I expect us to finish, despite an injury list dominated by central midfielders and defenders. It has reached the point where I am trying to track down Vladimir Romanov's spiritual healer, Rima, and persuade her to bring the golden stick to Oriam.

Vrancken is already hugely popular with the support. Winning his first Edinburgh derby in emphatic fashion at Easter Road certainly helped, but it is the direction he has restored that feels most significant. I cannot remember a recent Hearts manager uniting the fanbase quite so quickly.

The break should offer some much-needed breathing space. Getting Oisin McEntee , Malachi Fagan-Walcott and Ageu fit and up to speed would strengthen the squad before a gruelling run of twice-weekly fixtures as the European adventure begins.

Much has been said about the defence's inability to keep clean sheets. That may be a trade-off we have to accept under Vrancken, but midfield is the bigger concern.

Stuart Findlay and Harry Milne have struggled in recent matches, while the Laurent Mendy and Tomas Magnusson pairing does not give the defence enough support when Hearts build from the back.

Then there is Ageu. It is remarkable we still do not really know whether Hearts' record signing is any good. There was excitement around his debut at Livingston last season, but injuries have denied us enough evidence to form a fair judgement.

Nobody should pile pressure on a player who has spent so much of his Hearts career on the treatment table. Equally, if Jamestown Analytics identified him as worthy of a club-record fee, there is a reasonable expectation he can become a midfield mainstay.

His brief cameo at Kilmarnock offered little more than a reminder he exists. The extended break may finally give the Brazilian the chance to build fitness, find rhythm and show why Hearts invested so heavily.

Further forward, Calvin Miller and Josh McPake have made promising starts, while a settled partnership with JJ Williams or James Wilson could help Claudio Braga rediscover last season's form.

Hearts are not yet the finished article, but there is enough quality, momentum and belief to make this feel like the start of something exciting and, after too many false dawns, that is a prospect worth embracing.

articles.title: Jaxson Dart, Malik Nabers, Brian Burns and more Giants injury updates after Week 2 loss
articles.summary: The New York Giants saw four key players suffer injuries in the Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Here's injury updates on Jaxson Dart, Brian Burns, Malik...
articles.body:
The New York Giants were bitten by the injury bug on Monday night, with Jaxson Dart , Brian Burns , Andrew Thomas and Malik Nabers all coming down with injuries during the contest.

Dart suffered a scary knee injury on the first offensive series of the game for New York after getting sandwiched by two defenders and did not return.

Malik Nabers hurt his shoulder in the first half but was able to come back in the game and finish it out.

Andrew Thomas came down with a groin injury late in the fourth quarter and Brian Burns suffered an ankle injury not long after that.

Here's what we know about each player's status following the Week 2 loss to the Los Angeles Rams .

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo , Dart is believed to have suffered a sprained MCL and is "expected to miss some time."

Certainly great news considering we all feared the worst initially. Dart even tried to get back into the game, ESPN's Jordan Raanan reported, and was able to re-emerge from the locker room and finished out the game in street clothes on the sideline.

A sprained MCL could keep Dart out a handful of weeks, depending on the severity. We should know more on Tuesday.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh revealed that Brian Burns has a low-ankle sprain, according to SNY's Connor Hughes .

Another bullet dodged. Burns may only have to miss a few weeks, at most, with the injury.

There hasn't been much of an update on Thomas at this point.

Harbaugh did say, however, that none of the injuries sustained on Monday night are "life-threatening," per SNY , so it appears he'll be fine, also.

Nabers' injury occurred near the end of the first quarter and after the game he admitted he had to pop his shoulder back in before getting back into the game.

That said, Nabers feels like his shoulder will be OK, although he's set to have tests done just to make sure.

"My shoulder's okay. Gonna get an X-ray on it, see what's going on," Nabers said, according to SNY . "I was out there, trying to just come back out. We had lost Jax, so I didn't want to give the team another loss."

articles.title: WWE news: Ex-star makes 1st RAW appearance in 7 years
articles.summary: For the first time in nearly seven years, La Catalina, who is best known for her work in Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide, made an appearance on WWE Monday Night R...
articles.body:
For the first time in nearly seven years, La Catalina, who is best known for her work in Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide , made an appearance on WWE Monday Night RAW , marking her return to the red brand after almost seven years.

She competed in a Money in the Bank-qualifying match against Iyo Sky and Roxanne Perez. The Judgment Day member would ultimately win the match, but it marked Catalina's first match on RAW since Nov. 4, 2019, when she teamed up with Sin Cara to face Andrade and Zelina Vega.

Her return match pitted her against two of WWE's top women's division stars. Sky is a multi-time world champion, and Perez is a two-time NXT Women's Champion. It looked like Sky would seal the win by pinning Catalina, but Perez rolled her up for the pinfall.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Catalina is a professional wrestler who started competing long before her first WWE run started in 2019. She participated in a tryout for WWE in 2017 when she was 17. She signed a developmental deal once she turned 18, making her TV debut during the Nov. 4, 2019, edition of RAW.

She would hang around WWE for a couple more years, largely wrestling in NXT, Main Event, and 205 Live, but would leave in 2021.

In 2023, she joined Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre. She would hang around until April 2026, when she left the promotion. During her time in CMLL, she squared off with fellow Chilean wrestler and current Women's World Champion Stephanie Vaquer .

Catalina joined AAA by crashing Flammer's celebration on Apr. 11, 2026. At Triplemanía 34, she beat Flammer to win the Reina de Reinas Championship. This ended Flammer's 1,128-day reign.

articles.title: Emile Heskey on the reality of raising professional footballers: ‘It’s not my career, it’s theirs’
articles.summary: INTERVIEW: Former England striker Heskey has raised not one but two sons to professional level and speaks to Will Castle about what he got right as a footbal...
articles.body:
It's not particularly rare to see the offspring of an ex-professional follow in their parent's footsteps. Usually, though, it's just the one son or daughter that makes it. Two is quite the more remarkable.

Emile Heskey has managed to raise a pair of prodigies through the infamously perilous English academy system. His two sons, Jaden and Reigan, are professional footballers contracted to Manchester City . Eldest Jaden, 20, is on his second loan spell of the year at Sheffield Wednesday , while younger brother Reigan, 18, became the latest City starlet to make tried-and-tested venture to Germany this summer for his maiden loan away, joining Koln. Jadon Sancho, Jamie Gittens and Felix Nmecha are among those to tread the same path to great success, though City will be comforted by the knowledge that if Reigan experiences similar fortunes this term, they'll have him back next June.

Parenting footballers has become a topic of discussion over the past week, thanks to the media swirl surrounding 15-year-old Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel . Frankly, there has already been far too much coverage on what is the future of a child , while the focus on his father's allegedly difficult behaviour has gained significant traction despite the claims mostly being either social media hearsay or from reports citing unverified sources. The point of this piece is not to put more of a spotlight on either individual nor the rumours engulfing them.

What's conclusive, however, is Heskey's triumph in this field. He knows how to nurture the next generation.

Asked if football was always the dream for his sons, he tells The Independent : "I think so - you'd have to ask them!

"From a young age, Jaden wanted to play football. We took him aged three or four, and he just loved it. He loved going to the games. He loved the atmosphere. He loved everything about it. So then he was just programming himself to be the professional footballer that he wants to be.

"Reigan kind of just came along because he's the younger brother. But they've both been talented and they were lucky enough to go to an academy that helped with their progression, helped with their structure, helped with everything to make them the best possible players they could be. I think they were destined to do that."

Former England international Heskey, who turned out for the likes of Liverpool , Leicester and Aston Villa across a 22-year career, admits that his status as an ex-pro gave both his sons a foot in the door.

"100 per cent, there's no doubt that would help. That would give you, let's say, the upper hand," he says. From then, however, it's a level playing field.

"Then you've got to produce something, then you've got to really learn. And that was one of the good things about Jaden, he learns very, very quickly. He's very attentive to what the coaches are talking about. And like I said, Man City had some fantastic coaches."

The right type of coach is integral to an early rise. "This is where it all starts, when you're young - if you get a bad impression from them, it goes sour sometimes," asserts Heskey, who has joined forces with the Chase football coaching programme to try and inspire more into the profession. But just as important is the right type of parent.

Heskey says he never tried to be overbearing despite the obvious value of his playing experience. He also didn't let his own motivations take over: "That was easy - for me."

Instead, Heskey's approach was to keep his distance from the whole process. He didn't plaster them on his Instagram with nearly 100,000 followers, he didn't try and build their 'brand' while they were still in primary school.

"I always stood back," he said. "I never stood on the edge so my kids were looking over at me and thought I was overlooking them and scrutinising everything they did. I took a stance back, so that they never saw me - they weren't looking over so they could actually concentrate on the coaches' principles.

"It could be daunting for kids having their parents telling them certain things to do, but then the coach is telling them something else, so there's two different things that they've got going on.

"Sometimes you're best to take a step back because the reality is it's not my career, it's theirs."

Heskey has come across parents that are guilty of the opposite.

"When you look at pushy parents, who is it for? Is it for them or it it for the child?" he questions. "Because I don't think it's for the child, especially some of the times where [you hear] the way the parents talk to them.

"I generally wouldn't talk to my kids [about football] after training because I'd just let them do what they're doing. They're kids."

It got to a point when, during middle adolescence, Heskey had to turn up the intensity and start "grilling" his sons about their impending careers. This, however, led to something of a reality check for the 48-year-old former bagsman.

"I found out that they actually knew more than me," he admits, "because they'd been in an environment which taught them. I would actually be asking them certain things to try and pick their brain, because I was coaching then as well."

With both Jaden and Reigan now navigating the senior game, Heskey's 'less is more' formula holds weight on its own. But those who know the game best tend to agree with the approach. His ex-Liverpool team-mate Jamie Carragher , whose son James plays for Wigan Athletic , has also previously spoken about the damage "nightmare" parents can do to players with promise.

It turns out all you really need is faith, as Heskey finishes: "They're going to be big anyway, so just allow them to grow organically."

articles.title: ‘More of a relief…’ – Olivia Miles reacts to breaking Caitlin Clark’s rookie scoring record
articles.summary: Minnesota Lynx star Olivia Miles broke the rookie scoring record set by Caitlin Clark in 2024 with her incredible campaign in 2026. Miles was drafted with th...
articles.body:
Minnesota Lynx star Olivia Miles broke the rookie scoring record set by Caitlin Clark in 2024 with her incredible campaign in 2026.

Miles was drafted with the No. 2 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft and has instantly delivered for the Lynx, helping the contending franchise solidify themselves as title favorites this season.

Miles is averaging 19.8 points, 6.0 assists, and 4.7 rebounds this season, and her prolific scoring has led to her shattering Clark's rookie scoring record with two games in hand.

Olivia Miles is relieved after breaking Caitlin Clark's rookie scoring record

Miles spoke to reporters after her 21-point performance in the Lynx's win over the Connecticut Sun , expressing relief over breaking Clark's record and being able to put it in the rearview.

"It was more of a relief. Those things tend to loom over your head."

"It's special, but it means we're more so working well as a team. I have great teammates around me, great vets who allow me to be me out there. It wouldn't be possible without one, a coach that believes in you and then two, having teammates that have my back. So it's really special to obviously be able to accomplish that with such a great team and on a win as well."

Clark averaged 19.2 points (769 total points) as a rookie in 40 games, with Miles surpassing her in her 40th game of the season, ensuring nobody can claim she broke it because of having extra games available.

Miles and Clark will face off in the final two games of the season, as the Lynx and Fever end the regular season with two games against each other.

Clark's Fever need both wins to ensure they can remain in the fight for a top-four seed and avoid potentially falling to No. 8 in the standings.

The Lynx need one win to secure their status as the No. 1 seed for the 2026 WNBA Playoffs, so they will be motivated to eke out at least one result over their next two games, which will pit Clark and Miles against each other.

articles.title: Dave Portnoy tells the Pittsburgh Steelers they’re ‘wasting their time’ with Aaron Rodgers
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers need to find an answer to solve their offensive problems following an underwhelming start to the season. Mike McCarthy’s team has beg...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers need to find an answer to solve their offensive problems following an underwhelming start to the season.

Mike McCarthy's team has begun their season with one win and a loss, after their Week One victory was followed up with a dreadful showing against the New England Patriots on Sunday.

Aaron Rodgers was left frustrated on the back of Sunday's showing, and it is no surprise given the Steelers were only able to score a single field goal.

Dropped catches have been an issue for the Steelers, but Pittsburgh are also relying heavily on a 42-year-old in a league that is currently seeing mobile quarterbacks flourish.

In what will be Rodgers' final season in the NFL, Dave Portnoy has laid it all out for any Steelers fan hoping to see a postseason run with the veteran QB as the starter.

Dave Portnoy rips into Aaron Rodgers after Pittsburgh Steelers loss

Over the opening two weeks, the Steelers have only been able to score one receiving touchdown.

It has been a worrying start for McCarthy's offence, who look a real level below what would be expected from Rodgers .

"Why in the world, if you're the Pittsburgh Steelers, are you wasting your time with Aaron Rodgers? We only have so many years on this Earth," Portnoy said on Barstool.

"They're just wasting years. They have absolutely no chance of doing anything."

The Steelers will face the red-hot Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, who were able to hold the Houston Texans to just six points last weekend.

Seattle Seahawks fans have lapped up DK Metcalf's struggles in Pittsburgh after the Steelers traded for the wideout last year.

Drops from the wide receiver have not helped the Steelers at all, but it is clear that Portnoy believes a lot of the blame still lies with Rodgers.

articles.title: Patriots’ Mike Vrabel Reveals Concern Ahead Of Jaguars Matchup
articles.summary: The head coach spoke with the media followng their first win of the season.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots left Sunday's 20-3 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers feeling much better about their record and much worse about the condition of their roster. New England lost several players to injuries during the game, including safeties Craig Woodson and Dell Pettus . With the Patriots preparing to visit the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, the potential shortage at safety has become one of Mike Vrabel's most pressing concerns.

"We'll have to see where Craig is and where Dell is," Vrabel told reporters Monday. "Some of the veteran practice squad guys are going to factor in this week."

That could create an immediate opportunity for veteran Mike Brown or second-year safety Elliott Davison. Both are on the practice squad, and Brown has the added benefit of familiarity with Vrabel from their time together with the Tennessee Titans . The Patriots also may need more from Jaylen Reed , whom they acquired in an August trade. Reed played 28 defensive snaps against Pittsburgh after the injuries forced New England to adjust.

"I think he's been ready," Vrabel said of Reed. "He's tried to learn multiple positions."

That versatility suddenly matters quite a bit.

Woodson injured his shoulder during the third quarter and was later seen with his arm in a sling. Pettus departed with an ankle injury after getting hurt during a second-quarter punt.

Their uncertain availability comes at a difficult time. Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence has the talent to attack the middle of the field, and the Jaguars have multiple pass catchers capable of stressing a secondary.

New England's defense was the biggest reason it earned its first victory of the season. The Patriots held Pittsburgh to 235 total yards, limited the Steelers to a 2-for-12 performance on third down and did not surrender a touchdown. Christian Barmore forced an Aaron Rodgers fumble that Elijah Ponder returned 19 yards for a touchdown. The Patriots also intercepted Rodgers once and consistently prevented Pittsburgh from creating explosive plays.

Maintaining that standard in Jacksonville could require contributions from players who were not expecting prominent defensive roles this early in the season. The Patriots have Kevin Byard III available as the veteran leader of the group, but the situation around him could change considerably depending on the week's injury reports.

Vrabel did not offer firm timelines for Woodson or Pettus. His comments, however, made it clear that New England is already preparing alternatives. The Patriots proved against Pittsburgh that their defense can carry them through an uneven offensive performance. Sunday's trip to Jacksonville may reveal just how deep that defense truly is.

articles.title: Report: Jalen Duren Turns Down MEGA Offer as Contract Standoff Escalates
articles.summary: The Pistons reportedly offered Jalen Duren five years and $200 million, but the center remains unsigned with an October 1 deadline approaching.
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons have reportedly put $200 million on the table for Jalen Duren . It still has not produced an agreement.

Detroit increased its offer to five years and $200 million, up from the five-year, $190 million proposal reported earlier this month. According to The Athletic , the contract is fully guaranteed and contains no team option, player option or incentive language. Duren has rebuffed the proposal as the most consequential negotiation of the Pistons' offseason moves closer to a deadline.

The new offer represents a meaningful concession by Detroit. It also confirms that this dispute is no longer centered only on reaching the $200 million threshold. Duren's dissatisfaction reportedly dates to the approximately $20 million-per-season offer Detroit presented when he first became extension eligible.

The Pistons have moved considerably since then. Duren has not.

October 1 Now Becomes Detroit's Pressure Point

Duren has until October 1 to accept his one-year qualifying offer, although Detroit retains the ability to extend that deadline. The offer is worth $9.615 million and would allow Duren to play the 2026-27 season before becoming an unrestricted free agent next summer.

That route would carry significant risk for Duren. He would exchange $200 million in guaranteed money for one season of comparatively modest salary, betting that another strong year and good health would produce a larger contract in 2027. He would also receive the right to veto any trade after signing the qualifying offer.

The possibility has become increasingly credible. Duren was reportedly prepared to consider the qualifying-offer route before Detroit raised its proposal. The latest increase has not ended that threat.

Duren's Breakout Season Created This Price

Duren's leverage comes from a 2025-26 season in which he averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds, made his first All-Star team and earned third-team All-NBA honors. The NBA identified him as one of the summer's leading restricted free agents after helping Detroit win 60 games and secure the Eastern Conference's top seed.

His postseason created Detroit's counterargument. Duren's production dropped to 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds over 14 playoff games, and his limitations became harder to hide as opponents adjusted.

Detroit's $200 million offer pays Duren like a foundational player without approaching the five-year, $287 million supermax for which he became eligible. At $40 million annually, it also reaches the contract range his camp had reportedly targeted.

That is why the continued rejection changes the tenor of the negotiation. The remaining distance may involve money, but it also appears tied to how Duren believes Detroit valued him throughout the process.

The Pistons have consistently resisted facilitating a sign-and-trade, previously sending a firm message that they intended to retain Duren . Raising their offer to $200 million reinforces that commitment. It does not guarantee that the relationship can be repaired before October 1.

articles.title: Owen Valley golfer turns heartbreak into happiness at sectional
articles.summary: Redemption comes for junior Jacklyn Wheeler while North's team, South, Edgewood individuals punch tickets to regional
articles.body:
As Owen Valley's Jacklyn Wheeler stood in front of the board as the scorecards were filled in, a sense of relief and accomplishment washed over her.

Like last year, the margins were razor thin: every shot mattered. Unlike last year, she had to play only 18 holes , as her 94 made her the top individual qualifier in the Bloomington North girls golf sectional under cool, cloudy skies at Cascades Golf Course on Monday, Sept. 21.

She couldn't help but think back to this same time last year. The heartbreak she was determined to avoid.

"Oh my gosh, it was a surreal moment," she said. "I've thought about that moment all year. That's what I was spotting for today. I wanted to come back and win it."

Last year, at the end of a rain-soaked round, Wheeler and South's Kirin Bowden were forced into a playoff when both shot 97s. They each bogeyed the Quarry No. 9 hole on the first try. The second, Wheeler got stuck in a bunker and Bowden won the day.

Her head coach, Matt Beckwith, predicted before the season that the work she put in would give her a chance at redemption. On cue, she was the one this time who made the clutch shot on her last hole to become OV's first regional qualifier since Mariah Summers in 2017 .

"I was laying seven, and I had a putt from off the green," Wheeler said. "I made it. That shot was the best. It was off the green and at least a 20-footer, and I made it.

After a difficult start. Overnight rains crashed down, forcing the tournament to tee off at noon (instead of 8:30 a.m.) with a shotgun start. That eventually caused a backup, even with circle double-par rules in place, resulting in five-plus-hour rounds and the opportunity to lose patience and focus.

"The mental part of it was very difficult," Wheeler said. "You just had to keep a positive mentality. It was a great temperature out, it wasn't super hot. The course was in great shape for the conditions, I was actually expecting a lot worse than what it was.

"So I played good, but we just had to keep the mentality that whatever we got, we could battle through it."

And it is a 'we' thing to her with her family in tow all through the day, the same people responsible for the improvement she's made over the past year.

"Just the help of my parents and help from everybody around me," Wheeler said. "Just the way that I present myself through my parents. I want to carry my dad's name because he was a golfer, my mom was a golfer. To me, that means a lot. I want it for me and I want it for them.

Wheeler was one of three local golfers to advance as individuals

The host Cougars also made it out as a team with a second-place finish to the one team that seemed immune to the conditions. Martinsville won the title for the 33rd time with a 343, while also posting the top four scores of the day: Jocelyn Mercer, the medalist, at 82; Maddie Martin at 84; Lillian Lam at 86; and Olivia Hittel at 91.

North was second at 383, then came a dogfight for third that Bloomington South lost in heartbreaking fashion.

The Panthers and Columbus East each fired a 415 to keep Columbus North (416) and Indian Creek (417) at bay, but with Lizzy Yaley having to pull out with a back issue, that left only four golfers, allowing the Olympians to advance with a fifth score since there was no tie to break.

That left only senior Silvia Walker (96) to make the trip to the Legends for the Franklin Regional this Saturday and she'll be joined by Edgewood senior Libby McElhinney (97).

Wheeler and McElhinney had thoughts going in of making it out as individuals, knowing their teams would have a tough time cracking the top three. The Mustangs were seventh at 431, with OV next at 436, but will make it a run of three years in a row of being repped at regional.

McElhinney was the Western Indiana Conference medalist a couple of weeks ago, shooting a lifetime-best 79.

Back on her home course, McElhinney saw her score go up, but had to hang in on a day when she wasn't the only quality golfer working hard just to break 100.

"I think after the first few holes, I just had to keep my score manageable," McElhinney said. "I didn't play the best, but I realized I couldn't let my score go. When we got down to the end, I was thinking about a playoff."

McElhinney was a member of last year's first-ever Mustang team to qualify for regionals, so she knows the layout.

"She was coming off 13, just do the best you can because from what I hear everybody's saying, the scores are high," Edgewood coach Garry Lee said. "I'm happy for her. From where she was as a freshman to now, huge change."

Kate Johnson had a 93, and Ellie Bruce and Sadie Woodring each had 95s to lead the way for North, with Alli Rensi's 100 rounding out the effort.

"As a player, you don't really know where you fall," North coach Harrison Carmichael said. "And sometimes you might think that a shot didn't matter or this doesn't matter, and it all matters. Every shot does. If you reflect back on sectional for boys last year, it was a shot.

"That's always key to keep that in mind. Four and a half to five hours is a long time to keep the gas pedal down. But it's what's needed. We talk all year long about how this is the only day that matters."

Overall, the Cougars were three shots better than at the North Invite on a much drier, warmer day.

"Having more mature golfers, they all have the ability to what I call self-soothe," Carmichael said. "I don't feel the need, especially on their home course, to be there for every shot, or to be there when things are always hard.

"Because they've learned over the course of three or four years of varsity golf how to handle those situations."

Eastern Greene's Maddie Sylvester was the last individual qualifier out of the Bedford North Lawrence Sectional at Otis Park on Saturday.

The host stars ran away with the title for the 14th straight year, shooting a 357. Also moving on to the Terre Haute Regional at Hulman Links this Saturday were Seymour (393) and West Washington (460). Paoli was fifth (480), Orleans sixth (481), and Eastern Greene was seventh (487).

Sylvester shot a 109 to pace the T-Birds, with Izzi Forrester, a regional qualifier last year, shooting 117. Shelby Prince (123), Charlene Le Quere (138) and Baylee Meadows (140) rounded out Eastern's effort.

Emma Voris (79), Sammie Nusbaum (83), Kadynn Canada (91) and Bella Warren (104) topped BNL. Camley Whitfield of Paoli was the top individual qualifier with an 82, while Ava Hein of Trinity Lutheran shot a 106.

articles.title: Chad Tracy Delivers Powerful Message After Red Sox Clinch Playoff Spot
articles.summary: It was quite the turn around for the Red Sox, led by the masterful work of Tracy.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox did not clinch their postseason berth with a dramatic walk-off hit or a dominant performance from their pitching staff. They clinched after losing 5-1 to the Tampa Bay Rays and receiving help from Mike Yastrzemski and the Atlanta Braves .

Interim manager Chad Tracy did not care how the ticket was punched.

"When you work as hard as we have worked, I don't think you care much how it gets done," Tracy told reporters. "You just want to see your ticket get punched."

That message perfectly captured Boston's remarkable season. The Red Sox were 32-46 and appeared destined to spend the summer discussing trades, organizational changes and another disappointing finish. Instead, they became the first team in MLB history to finish above .500 and reach the playoffs after losing at least 46 of its first 78 games.

"They didn't take no for an answer," Tracy sai d.

Tracy inherited a 10-17 team when the Red Sox moved on from Alex Cora in April. There was no immediate transformation, and Boston's season continued to drift for several weeks.

Eventually, everything changed. Boston swept four games from the New York Yankees at Fenway Park in late June and began one of the most impressive turnarounds in franchise history. Young players developed into meaningful contributors, the clubhouse remained together and the Red Sox kept finding ways to survive injuries.

The result is a second consecutive postseason appearance and another likely Wild Card Series against the Yankees. That matchup did not work out for Boston last October. The Red Sox won the opener behind Garrett Crochet but dropped the next two games in New York.

This year's roster has traveled a much different road.

The Red Sox have played meaningful baseball for months because almost every loss threatened to undo the progress they had made. Players such as Roman Anthony , Payton Tolle and Connelly Early have grown up in that environment, while veterans including Trevor Story and Willson Contreras helped keep the clubhouse steady.

Now Boston has an opportunity to set its rotation, protect tired relievers and enter the postseason with more than a week to prepare. The final regular-season games still matter, especially with the Cleveland Guardians visiting Fenway Park. Boston can use the series to evaluate potential postseason matchups and determine which pitchers are best equipped for important October innings.

The celebration also strengthens Tracy's case to remain manager beyond this season. Boston did not merely improve after he took control. The Red Sox completed a turnaround that had never been accomplished in major league history.

Tracy did not want credit Sunday. His message remained focused on the players who refused to allow a terrible start to define them. That approach may be one of the biggest reasons the Red Sox are still playing.

articles.title: ESPN pinpoints Jaguars playoff 'downfall' after Week 2 loss
articles.summary: It's only Week 3, but ESPN's Ben Solak believes he may have identified what will be the Jacksonville Jaguars' downfall this season.
articles.body:
It's only Week 3, but ESPN's Ben Solak believes he may have identified what will be the Jacksonville Jaguars' downfall this season.

In Solak's latest "Seven things" article, one of the things he spends time pontificating on is the play of the Jaguars ' offensive and defensive lines, specifically, that those units will be a "problem" come the playoffs.

In Jacksonville 's most recent game against Denver , the Jaguars' offensive line unit faced a very good Broncos ' front and would struggle.

"Lawrence was pressured on 45.2% of his dropbacks and to great effect: He completed 33.3% of his pressured throws and 76.5% when unpressured," wrote Solak. "He had Denver's secondary beat when he had time."

Liam Coen addressed the offensive line play on Monday, noting that it wasn't just one player, but everyone contributed to the issues. He also mentioned that he and the coaching staff can do a better job helping that unit out, which includes quicker throws in certain situations and "moving the launch point."

On the other side of the ball, the Jaguars' pass rush struggled to get after Broncos ' quarterback Bo Nix . With time in the pocket, the Denver offense was able to generate numerous explosive plays through the air.

"Jacksonville had only a 19.4% pressure rate, less than half the 45.6% the Chiefs had in Week 1," Solak wrote. "And despite what you might expect, it was the Jaguars who blitzed more, at a 45% clip. Of their five second-half pressures, a half in which the Jaguars mostly led, four came on blitzes. Only one was in a four-down rush."

As Coen said , if the Jaguars are going to beat a team like Denver, then they have to create pressure.

The name of the game is getting after the quarterback and protecting the quarterback, and against a playoff-caliber team with high-end offensive and defensive line units, the Jaguars struggled to do both.

articles.title: Furlani officially departs Milan with new look directors in place
articles.summary: Giorgio Furlani is no longer part of Milan’s board, nearly four months after the club announced his dismissal as chief executive.According to TuttoMercatoWeb...
articles.body:
Giorgio Furlani is no longer part of Milan's board, nearly four months after the club announced his dismissal as chief executive.

According to TuttoMercatoWeb , the latest company registry filing confirms the Rossoneri's new corporate structure, with Furlani's name removed. Unlike coach Max Allegri, director Igli Tare and technical director Geoffrey Moncada, all of whom left their roles immediately, Furlani had remained formally within the organisation since May.

(Photo by PIF via Getty Images)

Calvelli installed as Milan chief executive to replace Furlani

Paolo Scaroni continues as board president, with Massimo Calvelli now in place as CEO. The remaining directors are Gerry Cardinale, Stefano Cocirio, Randy Levine, Riccardo Stefanelli, Robert Klein, David Castelblanco and Alfredo Craca.

The four men were removed together in a single statement from owners RedBird on May 25 , the day after a 2-1 home defeat to Cagliari on the final day cost Milan a place in the Champions League. The club branded the season an unequivocal failure, having needed only a point to secure a top-four finish.

Furlani had been on the board since 2019 before stepping up to chief executive in 2022, effectively representing former owners Elliott Management. Once Cardinale refinanced the vendor loan with Elliott, his role became surplus to requirements.

articles.title: Bloomington South girls soccer shows off scoring depth in win over North
articles.summary: Scoring is coming from some unexpected sources this year for the Panthers, who had to work to crack the Cougars' defensive shell.
articles.body:
On paper, this appeared to be a season where most of the Bloomington South girls soccer team's goals were going to come from Maddie Norman.

On turf, it hasn't played out that way at all. The junior, coming off a prolific 29-goal season, was hurt in the third match and missed the next six, forcing others to find the net. So far, 11 Panthers have scored, none with more than five goals to their credit, including Norman (one).

So maybe it's no real surprise that it was reserve freshman Kat Selo and veteran midfielder Chloe Trinidad who did the honors for South in a 2-0 win at Bloomington North on Monday, Sept. 21. It shows the balance and depth this team is developing.

"It's kind of been like this all year," Prall said. "Different people scoring every game.

"It's kind of the by-product of Maddie being out, and other people started scoring. We talked to Chloe about stepping up and adding goals this year, and she's done just that. The other games, she's been a bit more offensive and getting to her spots better. It's great. It's just about her growth and progression as a player. All game I thought she was dangerous. She was great."

Trinidad's goal came just seconds after a left-footed shot rolled a foot wide right of the net. She made sure the next was on target.

"It was great," Trinidad said. "My coach has been telling me to step it up and be a bigger leader on the team, so I think it was a great moment."

South's first goal was the kind it needed to break the ice against a stiff defense and keeper. Keeper Paloma Martinez worked to improve her leg strength on free kicks and was brought up to midfield with under three minutes to play in the first half.

"She's taking better and better free kicks that are dangerous," Prall said. "It's like a guard with shooting range in basketball, you have to guard more of the field and defend something else. She's had a great year."

Her Caitlin Clark-like boot from beyond the logo made it to the top of the box on one hop, ricocheted off a couple North defenders and into open space, where Selo pounced on it and scored. Unlucky for the Cougars, but just the thing the Panthers needed to ease the pressure a bit during halftime.

"They worked really hard (defensively)," North coach Samantha MacNeil said. "Our big thing we told them at halftime is, it happens, you've got to move on. And how we come back out will show the character of this team.

"They came out and played with a lot of heart and grit in that second half, especially."

It's also no shock that Trinidad and Malone, Norman and Addy Alexander (whose corner kicks were always on target) are the leaders in assists, with their ability to control the ball in traffic and be assertive defensively, causing turnovers. That was a big factor in the second half in shutting down most of North's potential attacks.

"This is one of the best ball-playing teams that we've had," Prall said. "Just as far as the ball moving."

So was jumping on the numerous goal kicks North keeper Isobel O'Leary had to send flying after each South shot attempt. Prall saw his team get more aggressive in one-timing those balls in the air back where they came from.

"We knew it was going to be a counter game for them," Prall said. "If we could have got that first ball, we just let it drop a couple times, and they got something going. We had numbers back, we just kept letting it hit the ground for no reason. It was a bit frustrating.

"But I thought we played pretty well the first half, too."

The last five regular season meetings with South have been over early: 5-0, 6-0, 8-0, 6-0, 4-0.

The offense was still a struggle for the Cougars, who mounted just a handful of dangerous counters against South's speedy defense, making Martinez work for a save just once.

"We were sitting a little bit more defensively, especially with how they were playing," MacNeil said. "So trying to get the ball and step up, something we didn't do as much as we should have, but we had great moments of doing that and it did create higher up chances for us."

North shut down shooting lanes and passing lanes and got a bushel of saves from O'Leary in goal.

"Izzy's been an absolute rockstar," MacNeil said. "She's been a captain for the past couple of seasons, so just great leadership from her."

For long stretches, the defense buckled down and made things tough for a tough opponent in a sectional-like atmosphere with something impotant on the line.. Less than a week after keeping Mid-State Conference leader Plainfield off the board for 73 minutes, they kept South frustrated despite ownership of the ball for most of the night.

"I'm sure it wears them down," MacNeil said. "But we have a defense that's no-quit and all heart, so they're going to keep giving us everything they've got."

articles.body:
Falkirk welcomed 17 new faces during a summer of major change, yet it is one of our existing players who has emerged as a standout performer heading into the first international break.

That man is Ethan Ross, who scored against St Johnstone last Saturday during another impressive and encouraging performance.

Ross was a key player as we worked our way through League One and the Championship. He played a particularly important role in our Championship-winning campaign, notably scoring twice on the final night of the season as victory over Hamilton clinched the title.

His first season in the Premiership never really got going after he suffered a bad injury against Livingston early in the campaign. However, the 25-year-old has clearly benefited from a full pre-season and a consistent run in the starting XI.

Filling the sizeable void left by Calvin Miller was always going to be a tough task, but Ross looks determined to give it his best shot.

As well as finding the net against St Johnstone, he drew the foul that resulted in Cheick Diabate being sent off.

Indeed, Ross is the second most fouled player during the opening stretch of the Premiership season, having been brought down 19 times.

It is not just his flair and attacking quality that add so much to the team. He is also a tireless worker who is always willing to track back and put in a shift.

It is great to see Ross flourishing and, on current form, I would like to think a contract extension is something the club are working on.

The Jaxson Dart injury on Monday night in the New York Giants 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams was devastating, but it may not be as bad as fans initially thought, and that may be thanks to some lip-reading off of the ESPN Monday Night Football broadcast.

Will Jaxson Dart miss the rest of the year?

We'll find out soon. But if that video above is an indication, he might miss a chunk of the year, which would be better than the entire year. Initial reports say he sprained his MCL in his knee.

articles.title: Why Giants aren't doomed if Jaxson Dart, Brian Burns miss signifigant time
articles.summary: The New York Giants’ 1-0 start suddenly feels like a distant memory after an injury-riddled 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. However, the most important ta...
articles.body:
The New York Giants ' 1-0 start suddenly feels like a distant memory after an injury-riddled 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams . However, the most important takeaway from Monday night is what happens next. Jaxson Dart went down with a left knee injury on the opening drive. Brian Burns later exited with an ankle injury. New York watched several other key players get banged up during an ugly night at SoFi Stadium. Yet the Giants still return home at 1-1. The initial news surrounding Dart is considerably better than the worst-case scenario. John Harbaugh said after the game that Dart's injury appeared to be "in the neighborhood" of an MCL sprain. Meanwhile, the quarterback's X-rays were negative. That matters, and it also leaves the Giants with a path forward.

Week 2 became an immediate lesson in survival for the Giants. Dart was injured just 11:20 into the first quarter when he was hit by Rams defenders while attempting a third-down pass. He ultimately did not return. Jameis Winston took over and completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception. New York failed to score a touchdown. The Giants' defense generated three takeaways, including two interceptions by Jevon Holland . Matthew Stafford and Davante Adams , however, eventually overwhelmed a depleted unit. Adams finished with seven catches for 184 yards and a touchdown. Burns then suffered his ankle injury late in the fourth quarter. That added another major concern to an already devastating night.

New York was outgained 439-147 , making the defeat considerably uglier than the final score alone suggests. Of course, this was also an extreme injury scenario. The Giants lost Dart, Burns, Malik Nabers and Andrew Thomas to injuries at various points. That left both sides of the roster compromised.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The biggest reason the Giants are not doomed is that Dart's injury has not been diagnosed as the season-ending catastrophe everyone initially feared. The early indication is an MCL sprain, although the Giants have not officially confirmed the diagnosis pending MRI results. Harbaugh acknowledged that avoiding the devastating outcome was encouraging. GM Joe Schoen said he expected Dart to be okay.

If Dart misses several weeks rather than the entire campaign, the Giants can approach September differently. The objective would be about surviving the temporary disruption, protecting the football, and allowing Dart to return when medically ready.

Burns' situation is similarly unresolved. His ankle injury occurred late in the game. Harbaugh has said that the initial diagnosis is a low ankle sprain . Still, the Giants will need further evaluation before determining the timetable. There is no basis yet to assume a long-term absence. That uncertainty is preferable to the assumption that one ugly night has permanently altered New York's season.

Replacing Dart is obviously a significant downgrade in mobility and explosiveness. Still, Winston does not need to become a superhero for the Giants. His performance against Los Angeles was poor. However, the circumstances were brutal. He entered cold on the road against one of the NFL's most disruptive defensive fronts. He was immediately forced to operate without the starting quarterback's established rhythm. Winston completed only 11 passes, but that single-game sample should not define what he can accomplish with a full week of preparation.

The Giants can also reduce the burden on him. Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris give New York a foundation for a more conservative, ball-control offense. Isaiah Likely can serve as a reliable middle-of-the-field option. If Nabers is able to recover from shoulder issues, the Giants would retain a legitimate explosive weapon on the perimeter.

The formula would be straightforward: run the football, protect Winston, manufacture completions, and let the defense keep games within reach. That is not spectacular, but it can still win games.

Losing Burns would create a bigger challenge defensively. That said, New York is not suddenly devoid of pass-rushing talent. Kayvon Thibodeaux remains capable of creating pressure from the edge. Dexter Lawrence continues to command attention in the interior. Abdul Carter also recorded his first sack of the season against Los Angeles .

The Rams exposed what happens when New York loses too many pieces simultaneously. That's particularly true after injuries hit the secondary and linebacker corps. However, that is different from asking the defense to play without Burns for several weeks while the rest of the unit remains intact. New York's defense just needs to keep opponents from running away.

The timing is another reason for optimism. After consecutive primetime games to open the season, the Giants return to MetLife Stadium on Sunday to face the 0-2 Tennessee Titans . New York then hosts Arizona before traveling to Washington . That does not guarantee victories, but it gives the Giants an opportunity to stabilize while Dart and Burns recover. The goal should be to remain competitive, avoid unnecessary risks, and get healthy.

The Giants looked completely overwhelmed Monday night, but one catastrophic evening does not erase the reasons they entered the season with optimism. Dart's injury still needs an MRI. Burns' timetable remains unknown. Those are significant questions, and pretending otherwise would be foolish. But neither player has been ruled out for the season. If the Giants can tread water while their two stars recover, they can still make a serious push once the roster gets healthier.

One of the top class of 2028 recruits has included the Wisconsin Badgers in his top four.

On Thursday, August 1, head coach Luke Fickell will learn if five-star EDGE Jalanie George is coming to Madison.

Rivals' Hayes Fawcett confirmed that George will be announcing his commitment in just over a weeks time, and the battle is down to Auburn, Miami, Washington, and Wisconsin.

According to Rivals , George is the No. 2 EDGE and No. 9 overall player in the class of 2028.

It's important to note that George plays for Desert Edge High School in Goodyear, Arizona.

When looking at the Badgers ' class of 2027 , commits Yahzeen Zion and Nathan Jones are both from the same school.

Wisconsin clearly has been building its pipeline in Goodyear for quite some time; now it's just a matter of whether or not they can land the first five-star in the Fickell era.
