articles.title: Army football determined to rebound at Temple after crushing loss
articles.summary: Army football is coming off a crushing loss to South Florida, but the Black Knights have to quickly bounce back with a trip to Temple this Friday.
articles.body:
Check out our Army football vs USF photo gallery: Best images

The feeling of shock and disappointment was palpable as the Army locker room had to absorb a crushing loss to South Florida on Sept. 12, spoiling what could have been a 2-0 start to the season.

The Bulls rallied for two touchdowns in the final 3:13 (the go-ahead score coming with 19 seconds left), erasing a 10-point deficit and escaping Michie Stadium with a 28-24 win.

In an Army minute, the elation of a thoroughly dominant 59-3 rout of FCS school Bryant a week earlier became a distant memory for the Black Knights .

As much as there was to dislike about dropping another one-score contest (Army was 4-5 in those close games a year ago), head coach Jeff Monken realizes there is a dual need to boost spirits, and yet drive the point home about shortcomings in the early stages of the season.

"There's got to be both,'' Monken said. "We have to find the positives as much as possible and encourage those behaviors and encourage the things that they're doing so well.

"We had some guys that played really well, and at times even guys that maybe made some mistakes, had plays where they played really well — we can point those out and highlight those (plays) and praise them for that. But then there's things that they can do better and we can do better collectively that we've got to point out so that the next time out more of those good things show up and fewer of the bad things do."

An early bye in the schedule last week may have come at the right time, especially with a "short week'' of preparation facing Army as it heads to Philadelphia for a rare Friday afternoon contest against Temple .

"I think any time there's a bye, it can be a positive in that the guys just get recovered a little bit,'' Monken said.

The season is only two games old, but that is following a month of preseason camp where a lot of players had to re-establish themselves or win open positions.

"Physically, it's a tough game ... it's a rugged, physical game, and guys get beat up certainly in competition,'' Monken said. "We practice really hard, we practice physical and we try to do that to prepare ourselves to play that way in a game — it's oftentimes the only thing that we really have that we feel like we can lean on.''

It should be noted this is the first of seven consecutive weeks of game action for Army, culminating with the all-important Air Force game on Nov. 7, a rare time there has been no bye week ahead of the contest with the Falcons.

Army is an early three-point favorite over Temple.

"We've just got to play the game hard, and we've got to play the game tough and physical if we're going to even give ourselves a chance,'' Monken said.

Chelsea have a defensive crisis which now spans several seasons, and no manager or player seems able to solve it.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

International breaks were tough at the best of times – now we've got a three week one, what on earth are we going to talk about? The Athletic have an idea – Simon Johnson has a long piece out about how to fix Chelsea.

Do they need fixing? Xabi Alonso has only just got his feet under the desk, but there are some pretty clear issues.

Chelsea's defensive excuses don't explain years of trouble

Levi Colwill (Photo by Darrian Traynor/Getty Images)

Clearly, improving the defence is priority number one. There's not point scoring if you can't keep a clean sheet, as we've found out in recent weeks. So far, none of Alonso's tinkering has worked. Neither a back four nor a back five has produced results.

Johnson's excuses are that – Emi Martinez and Maxence Lacroix are only just adjusting to the league. Levi Colwill is coming back from a long term injury. And there have been other players missing.

Yet you'd still expect far better, even with all those factors taken into account. We will give it until December for the likes of Lacroix, Colwill and Martinez to get up to speed, but after than we'll be starting to despair.

Emi Martinez has not had a good start to life at Chelsea – but there are some pretty shocking stats which provide him a good excuse for it.

Former Tottenham captain Ledley King has backed the current Spurs squad to turn their form around, insisting confidence will be key.

King believes there have been encouraging signs in recent performances, particularly during the opening stages of matches, but says Spurs have not made enough of their strongest periods.

"I'd say confidence is huge in football," King said, speaking after being inducted into Spurs' Hall of Fame.

"The last few games have been positive in terms of the performance, especially the start of the game. The first half has been good.

"But if you don't take your opportunities, and you know that there are so many good teams in this league, they're going to come back into the game and get their chances."

Stay up to date with all the latest Spurs news by joining our Tottenham WhatsApp channel .

King admitted Tottenham's failure to capitalise when on top has been the most frustrating aspect of their recent displays.

"That's the disappointing thing, that we've not been able to capitalise on our good periods," he added.

"All the lads can continue to do is keep believing in themselves, keep working hard, sticking together as a team.

"Most of them have been through some difficult periods in the last couple of seasons, and that's something they can draw on how to get out of this."

Reflecting on being part of the club's Hall of Fame, King added: "I always say that you think about the start of your career many times, but you don't think too much about the end of it, so for it to end this way, to be amongst some of the great players that are representing this football club is really humbling."

articles.title: Great Britain to face Alexander Zverev’s Germany in Davis Cup quarter-finals
articles.summary: Leon Smith’s side will face either Spain or Austria if they progress to the last-four
articles.body:
Great Britain will play Alexander Zverev 's Germany in the quarter-finals of the Davis Cup in November.

Britain booked their return to the eight-team Finals, this year held in Bologna, over the weekend with a 4-0 victory against Ecuador at London's Copper Box.

It is the first time Leon Smith 's side have reached the eight-team end-of-season event since 2023, when they fell at the first hurdle to Novak Djokovic 's Serbia.

The 2015 champions will have their work cut out to avoid the same fate given Zverev has shown a strong commitment to the competition, heading straight from winning his second grand slam title of the year at the US Open to Halle to help Germany defeat Croatia.

The Germans also have a very strong doubles pair in US Open finalists Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz but Zverev is their only top-50 singles player, which should give Britain encouragement.

Smith already knows he will be without Jack Draper , with the former world number four calling an end to his season because of an ongoing arm problem, but he will hope to have both Arthur Fery and Cameron Norrie available.

Norrie was a last-minute withdrawal against Ecuador because of a minor injury but Fery and debutant Toby Samuel won their singles matches before Britain's very strong doubles team of Henry Patten and Neal Skupski made sure of victory.

The Davis Cup Finals take place at the SuperTennis Arena from 24 to 29 November, with Britain lined up to play either Spain or Austria if they prevail against Germany.

Carlos Alcaraz did not play in the qualifiers this weekend but Spain still eased to victory over Chile and boast impressive strength in depth.

Hosts Italy are three-time defending champions having lifted the cup again last year despite the absence of world number one Jannik Sinner.

They will take on South Korea, the first Asian team to make the quarter-finals, while Czechia meet Canada in the other last-eight tie.

Playing the final stages of the tournament at one venue remains controversial, and Zverev criticised the format after Germany's win against Croatia, while Smith highlighted the fervent atmospheres in the ties between Czechia and USA and Canada and France.

"That example of what happened in Prague, and actually in Quebec as well, 10,500 people, I think it's really, really important to have that, because you won't get that in a 6,000-seater in Bologna," said the Scot.

articles.title: Man United injury woes worsen as two more withdraw from international duty
articles.summary: Four Man United players have withdrawn from duty on the first day of the extended international break
articles.body:
Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko has pulled out of Slovenia's squad as the club's injury woes compounded on a day of four international withdrawals.

The 23-year-old sat out Sunday's 1-1 draw at Fulham with a shin problem sustained in the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton last week.

As a result he will now not feature in two Nations League matches against Scotland , plus other games against North Macedonia and Switzerland .

" Manchester United can confirm that Benjamin Sesko has withdrawn from the Slovenia squad ahead of the upcoming three-week international break," said a United statement.

"Benjamin will undergo tests this week before defining his individual recovery plan."

Sesko later posted a statement on Instagram stating that he will commit himself to recovering from his shin issue.

"I am very sorry that I will have to miss the next matches of the national team," Sesko wrote.

"I have always played for Slovenia and will always play with heart and pride. The most important thing now is to fully dedicate myself to recovery.

"I am already working on getting back on the field as soon as possible and helping the national team and the club again.

"I believe in our boys, and I am sure that they will show the team spirit that has always adorned us this time.

"I can't wait to be able to wear the jersey with the national emblem again and, until then, I will be Slovenia's biggest fan."

Sesko became the fourth United player to withdraw from international duty on Monday, with goalkeeper Karl Darlow similarly leaving the Wales camp despite being on the bench for the Fulham game.

Darlow's exit was one third of the misery experienced by Craig Bellamy 's side, with Leeds star Harry Wilson forced out due to a quad injury, while Wrexham striker Nathan Broadhead has also been sidelined.

Sesko and Darlow join Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo on the early casualty list this international break, after the pair were among a five-man contingent to withdraw from the England squad .

Michael Carrick confirmed Rashford picked up an "issue" at Craven Cottage, with the forward substituted while appearing to be struggling with his hip – which was a persistent issue over the summer.

Midfielder Mainoo, who travelled to this summer's World Cup but did not play a single minute of the tournament under Tuchel, was also substituted during the closing stages of the draw.
